name: Leonidas of Tarentum
bio: Leonidas of Tarentum, a Hellenistic epigrammatist of the early third century BC, is known for epitaphs and for dedications by poor country folk and craftsmen, often with a touch of humour about poverty.
In this archive every epigram that Paton heads simply “Leonidas” is filed here; the isopsepha of Leonidas of Alexandria (Book VI, 321–329) are not included.

poems.title: Book V, 188
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: It is not I who wrong Love. I am gentle, I call Cypris to witness ; but he shot me from a treacherous bow, and I am all being consumed to ashes. One burning arrow after another he speeds at me and not for a moment does his fire slacken. Now I, a mortal, shall avenge myself on the transgressor though the god be winged. Can I be blamed for self-defence ?

poems.title: Book V, 206
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Meto and Satyra, the daughters of Antigenides, now advanced in age, the willing work-women of the Muses, dedicate to the Pimpleian Muses, the one her swift-lipped flute and this its box-wood case, and Satyra, the friend of love, her pipe that she joined with wax, the evening companion of banqueters, the sweet whistler, with which all night long she waited to see the day dawn, fretting not because the portals would not open.

poems.title: Book VI, 4
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Diophantus the fisherman, as is fit, dedicates to the patron of his craft these relics of his old calling, his hook, easily gulped down, his long poles, his line, his creels, this weel, device of sea-faring netsmen for trapping fishes, his sharp trident, weapon of Poseidon, and the two oars of his boat.

poems.title: Book VI, 13
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Huntsman Pan, the three brothers dedicated these nets to thee, each from a different chase: Pigres these from fowl, Damis these from beast, and Clitor his from the denizens of the deep. In return for which send them easily caught game, to the first through the air, to the second through the woods, and to the third through the shore-water.

poems.title: Book VI, 35
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: This skin did Teleso stretch on the woodland plane-tree, an offering to goat-hoofed Pan the goattreader, and the crutched, well-pointed staff, with which he used to bring down red-eyed wolves, the cheese-pails, too, and the leash and collars of his keen-scented hounds.

poems.title: Book VI, 44
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.note: Paton marks the attribution with a query.
poems.text: To the must-bibbing Satyrs and to Bacchus the planter of the vine did Heronax consecrate these three casks of fresh wine filled from three vineyards, the first-fruits of his planting. We, having first poured what is right from them to purple Bacchus and the Satyrs, will drink more than the Satyrs.

poems.title: Book VI, 120
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Not only do I know how to sing perched in the high trees, warm in the midsummer heat, making music for the wayfarer without payment, bad feasting on delicate dew, but thou shalt see me too, the cicada, seated on helmeted Athene’s spear. For as much as the Muses love me, I love Athene ; she, the maiden, is the author of the flute.

poems.title: Book VI, 129
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Eight shields, eight helmets, eight woven coats of mail and as many blood-stained axes, these are the arms, spoil of the Lucanians, that Hagnon, son of Euanthes, the doughty fighter, dedicated to Coryphasian Athene.

poems.title: Book VI, 130
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The shields, spoils of the brave Gauls, did Molossian Pyrrhus hang here as a gift to Itonian Athene, after destroying the whole army of Antigonus. Tis no great wonder! Now, as of old, the sons of Aeacus are warriors.

poems.title: Book VI, 131
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: These great shields won from the Lucanians, and the row of bridles, and the polished double-pointed spears are suspended here to Pallas, missing the horses and the men their masters; but them black death hath devoured.

poems.title: Book VI, 188
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Therimachus the Cretan suspended these his hare-staves to Lycaean Pan on the Arcadian cliff. But do thou, country god, in return for his gift, direct aright the archer’s hand in battle, and in the woe We de” forest dells stand beside him on his right hand, giving him supremacy in the chase and supremacy over his foes.

poems.title: Book VI, 200
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Ilithyia, at thy glorious feet Ambrosia, saved from the bitter pangs of labour, laid her head-bands and her robe, because that in the tenth month she brought forth the double fruit of her womb.

poems.title: Book VI, 202
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Atthis hung over thy virginal portals, O daughter of Leto, her tasselled zone and this her frock, when thou didst deliver her heavy womb of a live child.

poems.title: Book VI, 204
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Theris, the cunning worker, on abandoning his craft, dedicates to Pallas his straight cubit-rule, his stiff saw with curved handle, his bright axe and plane, and his revolving gimlet.

poems.title: Book VI, 205
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: These are the tools of the carpenter Leontichus, the grooved file, the plane, rapid devourer of wood, the line and ochre-box, the hammer lying next them that strikes with both ends, the rule stained with ochre, the drill-bow and rasp, and this heavy axe with its handle, the president of the craft; his revolving augers and quick gimlets too, and these four screw-drivers and his double-edged adze—all these on ceasing from his calling he dedicated to Athene who gives grace to work.

poems.title: Book VI, 211
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Callicleia, her wish having been granted, dedicates in thy porch, true Cypris, the silver statuette of Love, her anklet, the purple caul of her Lesbian hair, her pale-blue bosom-band, her bronze mirror, and the broad box-wood comb that gathered in her locks.

poems.title: Book VI, 221
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Through the wintry night and driving hail, flying from the snow and bitter frost, a lion old and solitary and indeed stricken in all its limbs came to the fold of the goat-herds who haunt the cliffs. They, no longer anxious for their goats, but for themselves, sat calling on Zeus the Saviour. But the beast, the beast of the night, waiting till the storm was past, went away from the fold without hurting man or beast. To Pan the god of the mountain peaks they dedicated on this thick-stemmed oak this welllimned picture of what befel them.

poems.title: Book VI, 226
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: This is Clito’s little cottage, this his little strip of land to sow, and the scanty vineyard hard by, this is his patch of brushwood, but here Clito passed eighty years.

poems.title: Book VI, 262
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The beast which wrought havoc on the flock and the cattle-pen and the herdsmen, and feared not the loud noise of the dogs, Eualces the Cretan slew while shepherding his flock at night, and hung on this pine.

poems.title: Book VI, 263
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Sosus, rich in cattle, lenched this tawny lion, which he slew with his spear just as it had begun to devour the suckling calf, nor went it back from the sheepfold to the wood. To the calf the brute transpierced paid blood for blood, and sorrowful to it was the murder it wrought.

poems.title: Book VI, 281
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Great Mother, who watchest over Dindyma and the hills of Burnt Phrygia,® bring, O sovereign lady, little Aristodike, Silene’s daughter, up to an age ripe for marriage and the hymn of Hymen, the due end of girlhood. For this, dancing at many a festival held in thy courts and before thy altar, she tossed this way and that her virgin hair.

poems.title: Book VI, 286
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The right end of the border, measuring a span and a whole palm, is the work of Bitto; the other extremity was added by Antianira, while Bitie worked the girls and the Maeander? in the middle. Artemis, fairest of the daughters of Jove, take to thy heart this piece of woven work which the three vied in making.

poems.title: Book VI, 288
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: We, the industrious daughters of Lycomedes, Atheno, Melitea, Phinto, and Glenis, offer from the tithe of our work, as a gift to please thee, a little part of the little we have in our poverty, the laborii Altogether twelve finger’s breadths. ous spindle, the weaving-comb that passes between the threads of the warp, sweet songster of the loom, our round spools, our... ., and our heavy weaving-blade. Fill our hands, Athene, ever after, and make us rich in meal instead of poor in meal,

poems.title: Book VI, 289
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Autonoma, Melite, and Boiscion, the three Cretan daughters of Philolaides and Nico, dedicated in this temple, O stranger, as a gift to Athene of the spool on ceasing from the labours of Athene, the first her thread-making ever-twirling spindle, the second her wool-basket that loves the night, and the third her weaving-comb, the industrious creator of raiment, that watched over the bed of Penelope.

poems.title: Book VI, 293
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The staff and these slippers hang here, Cypris, the spoils won from Sochares the cynic; his grimy oil-flask, too, and the remains of his wallet all in holes, stuffed full of ancient wisdom. They were dedicated here, on thy begarlanded porch, by comely Rhodon, when he caught the all-wise greybeard.

poems.title: Book VI, 296
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Sosippus gives to Hermes, now that he has outswum the greater part of his strength and the feebleness of old age fetters him, his securely fixed trap, his cane springes, his nets, this curved hare-club, his quiver, this quail-call, and the well-woven net for throwing over wild fowl.

poems.title: Book VI, 298
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: A wallet, a hard untanned goat-skin, this walking-stick, an oil-flask never scraped clean, a dog-skin purse without a copper in it, and the hat, the covering of his impious head, these are the spoils of Sochares that Famine hung on a tamarisk bush when he died.

poems.title: Book VI, 300
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Latonian goddess, accept these offerings from Leonidas the wanderer, the pauper, the flour-less: rich barley-cakes, olives easy to store, and this green fig from the tree. Take, too, lady, these five grapes picked from a rich cluster, and this libation of the dregs of the cup. But if,as thou hast saved me from sickness so thou savest me from hateful penury, await a sacrifice of a kid.

poems.title: Book VI, 302
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Out of my hut, ye mice that love the dark! Leonidas’ poor meal-tub has not wherewith to feed mice. The old man is contented if he has salt and two barley-cakes. This is the life I have learnt to acquiesce in from my fathers. So why dost thou dig for treasure in that corner, thou glutton, where thou shalt not taste even of the leavings of my dinner? Haste and be off to other houses (here is but scanty fare), where thou shalt win greater store.

poems.title: Book VI, 305
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: To Gluttony and Voracity, the deities who love well flavoured sauces, did Dorieus who stinks of... English equivalent. ‘The thrissa is a fish that goes in shoals, a little like mackerel and not particularly bony ; the chalkis is a kind of bream. dedicate these enormous Larissean boiling cauldrons, the pots and the wide-gaping cup, the well-wrought curved flesh-hook, the cheese-scraper, and the soup-stirrer. Gluttony, receive these evil gifts of an evil giver, and never grant him temperance.

poems.title: Book VI, 309
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: To Hermes Philocles here hangs up these toys of his boyhood: his noiseless ball, this lively boxwood rattle, his knuckle-bones he had such a mania for, and his spinning-top.

poems.title: Book VI, 334
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Caves and holy hill of the Nymphs, and springs at the rock’s foot, and thou pine that standest by the water; thou square Hermes, son of Maia, guardian of the sheep, and thou, Pan, lord of the peak where the goats pasture, graciously receive these cakes and the cup full of wine, the gifts of Neoptolemus of the race of Aeacus.

poems.title: Book VI, 355
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: His mother, being poor, gives Micythus’ picture to Bacchus, poorly painted indeed. Bacchus, I pray thee, exalt Micythus; if the gift be trumpery, it is all that simple poverty can offer.

poems.title: Book VII, 13: On the Same
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.note: Attribution doubtful in Paton (Leonidas or Meleager).
poems.text: As Erinna, the maiden honey-bee, the new singer in the poets’ quire, was gathering the flowers of the Muses, Hades carried her off to wed her. That was a true word, indeed, the girl spoke when she lived: “Hades, thou art an envious god.”

poems.title: Book VII, 19: On the Same
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Alcman the graceful, the swan-singer of wedding hymns, who made music worthy of the Muses, lieth in this tomb, a great ornament to Sparta, or perhaps at the last he threw off his burden and went to Hades. (The last couplet is quite obscure as it stands. )

poems.title: Book VII, 35: On the Same
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Congenial to strangers and dear to his countrymen was this man, Pindar, the servant of the sweet-voiced Muses.

poems.title: Book VII, 67: On the Same
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Mournful minister of Hades, who dost traverse in thy dark boat this water of Acheron, receive me, Diogenes the Dog, even though thy gruesome bark is overloaded with spirits of the dead. My luggage is but a flask, and a wallet, and my old cloak, and the obol that pays the passage of the departed. All that was mine in life I bring with me to Hades, and have left nothing beneath the sun.

poems.title: Book VII, 163
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: A. “Who art thou, who thy father, lady lying under the column of Parian marble?” B. “Praxo, daughter of Calliteles.” A. “And thy country?” B. “Samos.” A. “Who laid thee to rest?” B. “Theocritus to whom my parents gave me in marriage.” A. “And how didst thou die?” B. “In childbirth.” A. “How old?” B. “Twenty-two.” A. “Childless then?” B. “No! I left behind my three year old Calliteles.” A. “May he live and reach a ripe old age.’ B. “And to thee, stranger, may Fortune give all good things.”

poems.title: Book VII, 198
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Wayfarer, though the tombstone that surmounts my grave seems small and almost on the ground, blame not Philaenis. Me, her singing locust, that used to walk on thistles, a thing that looked like a straw, she loved and cherished for two years, because I made a melodious noise. And even when I was dead she cast me not away, but built this little monument of my varied talent.

poems.title: Book VII, 264
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: A good voyage to all who travel on the sea; but let him who looses his cable from my tomb, if the storm carries him like me to the haven of Hades, blame not the inhospitable deep, but his own daring.

poems.title: Book VII, 266
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: I am the tomb of the shipwrecked Diocles. Out on the daring of those who start from here, loosing their cable from me!

poems.title: Book VII, 273
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The fierce and sudden squall of the south-east wind, and the night and the waves that Orion at his dark setting arouses were my ruin, and I, Callaeschrus, glided out of life as I sailed the middle of the Libyan deep. I myself am lost, whirled hither and thither in the sea a prey to fishes, and it is a liar, this stone that rests on my grave.

poems.title: Book VII, 283
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Way, roaring sea, didst thou not cast me up, Phyleus, son of Amphimenes, when I came to a sad end, far away from the bare beach, so that even wrapped in the evil mist of Hades I might not be near to thee?

poems.title: Book VII, 295
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Theris, the old man who got his living from his lucky weels, who rode on the sea more than a gull, the preyer on fishes, the seine-hauler, the prober of crevices in the rocks, who sailed on no many-oared ship, in spite of all owed not his end to Arcturus, nor did any tempest drive to death his many decades, but he died in his reed hut, going out like a lamp of his own accord owing to his length of years. This tomb was not set up by his children or wife, but by the guild of his fellow fishermen.

poems.title: Book VII, 316
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.note: Attribution doubtful in Paton (Leonidas or Antipater).
poems.text: Pass by my monument, neither greeting me, nor asking who I am and whose son. Otherwise mayst thou never reach the end of the journey thou art on, and if thou passest by in silence, not even then mayst thou reach the journey’s end.

poems.title: Book VII, 408
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Go quietly by the tomb, lest ye awake the malignant wasp that lies asleep; for only just has it been laid to rest, the spite of Hipponax that snarled even at his parents. Have a care then; for his verses, red from the fire, have power to hurt even in Hades.

poems.title: Book VII, 422
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: What shall we conjecture about you, Pisistratus, when we see a Chian die carved on your tomb?? Shall we not say that you were a Chian? That seems probable. Or shall we say that you were a gamester and not a particularly lucky one, my friend? Or are we still far from the truth, and was your life’s light put out by Chian wine? Yes, I think now we are near it.

poems.title: Book VII, 440
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: O Tomb, what a man was he, the dead whose bones thou dost hide in the night: O earth, what a head thou hast engulphed! Very pleasing was Aristocrates to the flaxen-haired Graces; much is his memory treasured by all. Aristocrates could converse sweetly, without a frown, and over the wine he could guide well the convivial flow of talk; and well he knew how to confer kindness on compatriots and strangers. Such, beloved earth, is the dead who is thine.

poems.title: Book VII, 448
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The tomb is that of Protalidas of Lycastus who was supreme in love, war, the chase and the dance. Ye judges of the under-world, yourselves Cretans, ye have taken the Cretan to your company.

poems.title: Book VII, 452
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Remember temperate Eubulus, ye passers-by. Let us drink, we all end in the haven of Hades.

poems.title: Book VII, 455
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Wine-sipping old Maronis, the jar-drier, lies here, and on her tomb, significant to all, stands an Attic cup. She laments beneath the earth not for her husband and children whom she left in indigence, but solely because the cup is empty.

poems.title: Book VII, 463
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: This is Timoclea, this is Philo, this is Aristo, this is Timaetho, the daughters of Aristodicus, all dead in childbirth. Their father Aristodicus died after erecting this monument to them.

poems.title: Book VII, 466
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: O unhappy Anticles, and I most unhappy who have laid on the pyre my only son in the bloom of his youth! At eighteen didst thou perish, my child, and I weep and bewail my old age bereft of thee. Would I could go to the shadowy house of Hades! Nor dawn nor the rays of the swift sun are sweet to me. Unhappy Anticles, gone to thy doom, be thou healer of my mourning by taking me away from life to thee.

poems.title: Book VII, 472
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: O man, infinite was the time ere thou camest to the light, and infinite will be the time to come in Hades. What is the portion of life that remains to thee, but a pin-prick, or if there be aught tinier than a pin-prick? A little life and a sorrowful is thine; for even that little is not sweet, but more odious than death the enemy. Men built as ye are, of such a frame of bones, do ye lift yourselves up to the air and the clouds? See, man, how little use it is; for at the end of the thread a worm seated on the loosely woven vesture reduces it to a thing like a skeleton leaf, a thing more loathly than a cobweb. Enquire of thyself at the dawn of every day, O man, what thy strength is and learn to lie low, content with a simple life; ever remembering in thy heart, as long as thou dwellest among the living, from what stalks of straw thou art pieced together.’

poems.title: Book VII, 472b
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Avoid the storms of life and hie ye to the haven, to Hades, as I, Pheidon the son of Critas, did.

poems.title: Book VII, 478
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Who ever canst thou be? Whose poor bones are these that remain exposed beside the road in a coffin half open to the light, the mean tomb and monument ever scraped by the axle and wheel of the traveller’s coach? Soon the carriages will crush thy ribs, poor wretch, and none to shed a tear for thee.

poems.title: Book VII, 480
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Already, Sirrah, my bones and the slab that lies on my skeleton are exposed and crushed, already the worms are visible, looking out of my coffin. What avails it to clothe ourselves with earth; for men travelling over my head have opened here a road untrodden before. But I conjure you by the infernal powers, Pluto, Hermes and Night, keep clear of this path.

poems.title: Book VII, 503
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: A. “O stone standing a burden on the ancient beach, tell me whom thou holdest, whose son and whence.” B. “Phinto the son of Bathycles of Hermione, who perished in the heavy sea, encountering the blast of Arcturus.”

poems.title: Book VII, 504
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Pammis, Callignotus’ son, the shore-fisher, a first class hand at catching wrasse and scaros and the perch, greedy seizer of the bait, and all fish that live in crevices and on rocky bottoms, met his death by biting a rock-dwelling iulis from his first catch of the day, a fish he lifted from the sea for his destruction; for slipping from his fingers, it went wriggling down his narrow gullet. So breathed he his last, rolling over in agony, near his lines, rod, and hooks, fulfilling the doom the destinies spun for him, and Gripo the fisherman built him this tomb.

poems.title: Book VII, 506
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: I am buried both on Jand and in the sea; this is the exceptional fate of Tharsys, son of Charmides. For diving to loosen the anchor, which had become fixed, I descended into the Ionian sea; the anchor I saved, but as I was returning from the depths and already reaching out my hands to the sailors, I was eaten; so terrible and great a monster of the deep came and gulped me down as far as the navel. The half of me, a cold burden, the sailors drew from the sea, but the shark bit off the other half. On this beach, good Sir, they buried the vile remains of Tharsys, and I never came home to my country.

poems.title: Book VII, 648
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Good Aristocrates, as he was taking ship for Acheron, resting his doomed head on his hand, said: “Let every man seek to have children and get him a wife, even if miserable poverty pinch him. Let him support his life with pillars; a house without pillars is ill to look on. Nay what is best, may the room where his hearth is have many fair columns, and shining with the luxury of many lights, illumine the log that burns on the hearth.”

poems.title: Book VII, 652
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Thou booming sea, why didst thou rise in angry storm, and striking with a huge wave send headlong to the deep, cargo and all, Teleutagoras, son of Timares, as he sailed in his little ship? He, lying somewhere dead on the broad beach, is bewailed over by terns and fish-eating gulls, and Timares, looking on his son’s empty tear-bedewed tomb, weeps for his child Teleutagoras.

poems.title: Book VII, 654
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The Cretans are ever brigands and pirates, and never just; who ever heard of the justice of a Cretan? So they were Cretans who threw me unhappy Timolytus into the sea, when I was travelling with no very rich cargo. I am bewailed by the seagulls, and there is no Timolytus in this tomb.

poems.title: Book VII, 655
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: A little dust of the earth is enough for me, and may a rich and useless monument, a weight ill for the dead to bear, crush some other man in his rest. What is that to Alexander, son of Calliteles, if they know who I am or not, now that I am dead?

poems.title: Book VII, 656
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Salute, Sir, this little mound and modest monument of hapless Alcimenes, though it be all overgrown by the sharp buckthorn and brambles on which I, Alcimenes, once waged war.

poems.title: Book VII, 657
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Ye shepherds who roam over this mountain ridge feeding your goats and fleecy sheep, do, in the name of Earth, a little kindness, but a pleasant one, to Cleitagoras, for the sake of Persephone underground. May the sheep bleat to me, and the shepherd seated on the unhewn rock pipe soft notes to them as they feed, and may the villager in early spring gather meadow flowers and lay a garland on my grave. May one of you bedew it with the milk of a ewe, mother of pretty lambs, holding her udder up and wetting the edge of the tomb. There are ways, I assure you, even among the dead of returning a favour done to the departed.

poems.title: Book VII, 660
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Stranger, a Syracusan named Orthon enjoins this upon thee: “Never go out drunk on a winter night.” For that was what caused my death, and instead of resting in my ample country I lie clothed in foreign soil.

poems.title: Book VII, 661
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The tomb is that of Eusthenes the sophist, who was a reader of character, skilled in discovering our thought from our eyes. Well did his companions bury him, a stranger in a strange land, and among them was a poet marvellously dear to him. So the sophist, although he was feeble, had those who took care that he should have on his death all proper honour.

poems.title: Book VII, 662
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The girl is gone to Hades before her time in her seventh year, before all her many playmates, hapless child, longing for her little brother, who twenty months old tasted of loveless death. Alas Peristera for thy sad fate! How hath Heaven decreed that the very path of men should be sown with calamities!

poems.title: Book VII, 663
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Little Medeus made this tomb by the wayside for his Thracian nurse, and inscribed it with the name of Clita. She will have her reward for nursing the boy. Why? She is still called useful”!

poems.title: Book VII, 665
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Trust not in the length or depth of the ship thou voyagest in; one wind lords it over every keel. One blast destroyed Promachus, and one huge wave dashed him into the trough of the sea. Yet Heaven was not entirely unkind to him, but he got funeral and a tomb in his own country by the hands of his own people, since the rude sea cast out his body on the expanse of the beach.

poems.title: Book VII, 715
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Far from the Italian land J lie, far from my country Tarentum, and this is bitterer to me than death. Such is the life of wanderers, ill to live; but the Muses loved me and instead of sourness sweets are mine. The name of Leonidas hath not sunk into oblivion, but the gifts of the Muses proclaim it to the end of days.

poems.title: Book VII, 719
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: I am the tomb of Tellen, and under ground I hold the old man, who was the first to learn how to compose comic songs.

poems.title: Book VII, 726
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Old Platthis often repelled from her her evening and morning sleep, keeping poverty away, and near the door of gray old age used to sing a tune to her spindle and familiar distaff. Still by the loom until the dawn she revolved in company with the Graces that long task of Pallas, or, a loveable figure, smoothed with her wrinkled hand on her wrinkled knee the thread sufficient for the loom. Aged eighty years comely Platthis who wove so well set eyes on the lake of Acheron.

poems.title: Book VII, 731
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: “I am already supported only ona stick, like a vine on a stake; Death calls me to Hades. Stop not thy ears, Gorgus. What further pleasure hast thou in basking in the sun yet for three or four summers?” So speaking in no braggart strain the old man cast away his life and settled in the abode of the greater number.

poems.title: Book VII, 736
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Vex not thyself, O man, leading a vagrant life, rolled from one land to another. Vex not thyself if thou hast a little hut to cover thee, warmed by a little fire, if thou hast a poor cake of no fine meal kneaded by thy hands in a stone trough, if thou hast mint or thyme for a relish or even coarse salt not unsweetened.

poems.title: Book VII, 740
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: I am the stone that rests on Cretho and makes known his name, but Cretho is ashes underground, he who once vied with Gyges in wealth, who was lord of many herds and flocks, who was—why need I say more he who was blessed by all. Alas, what a little share of his vast lands is his!

poems.title: Book IX, 24
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: As the burning sun, rolling his chariot-wheels, dims the stars and the holy circle of the moon, so Homer, holding on high the Muses’ brightest torch, makes faint the glory of all the flock of singers.

poems.title: Book IX, 25
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: This is the book of learned Aratus, whose subtle mind explored the long-lived stars, both the fixed stars and the planets with which the bright revolving heaven is set. Let us praise him for the great task -at which he toiled ; let us count him second to Zeus, in that he made the stars brighter.

poems.title: Book IX, 99
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The nanny-goat’s nimble, bearded spouse once in a vineyard nibbled all the tender leaves of a vine. The vine spoke thus to him from the ground: “Cut close with thy jaws, accursed beast, my fruitful branches; my stem is entire, and shall again send forth sweet nectar enough to serve as a libation for thee, goat, when thou art sacrificed.” +

poems.title: Book IX, 316
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: O ve who pass along this road, whether ye are going from town to the fields or returning to the city from the country, we two gods here are the guardians of the boundary. I, as you see me, am Hermes, and this other fellow is Heracles.1 We both are gracious to mortals, but to each other—save the mark! If anyone offers a dish of wild pears to both of us, ke bolts them. Yes, and indeed, likewise grapes; whether they are ripe ones or any quantity of sour ones, he stows them away. I detest this method of going shares, and get no pleasure from it. Let whoever brings us anything serve it separately to each of us and not to both, saying, “This is for thee, Heracles,” and again, “This is for Hermes.” So he might make up our quarrel.

poems.title: Book IX, 318
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Dear Hermes, whose are this hillside rich in fennel and chervil, and this goat-pasture? Be kind both to the gatherer of herbs and to the goatherd, and thou shalt have thy share of both the herbs and the milk.

poems.title: Book IX, 320
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Eurotas said once to Cypris, “Either arm thyself or go out of Sparta. The town has a craze for arms.” She smiled gently and replied, “I will both remain always unarmed and continue to dwell in the land of Lacedaemon.” Our Cypris is unarmed as elsewhere, and these are shameless writers who declare that with us even the goddess bears arms.

poems.title: Book IX, 322
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: These spoils are not mine. Who hung this unwelcome gift on the walls of Ares? Unbruised are the helmets, unstained by blood the polished shields, and unbroken the frail spears. My whole face reddens with shame, and the sweat, gushing from my forehead, bedews my breast. Such ornaments are for a lady’s bower, or a banqueting-hall, or a court, or a bridal chamber. But blood-stained be the cavalier’s spoils that deck the temple of Ares; in those I take delight.

poems.title: Book IX, 326
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Hail, thou cold stream that leapest down from the cloven rock, and ye images of the Nymphs carved by a shepherd’s hand! Hail, ye drinking troughs and your thousand little dolls, ye Maidens of the spring, that lie drenched in its waters! All hail! And I, Aristocles, the wayfarer, give you this cup which I dipped in your stream to quench my thirst.

poems.title: Book IX, 329
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Ye water Nymphs, children of Dorus, water diligently this garden of Timocles, for to you, Maidens, doth the gardener Timocles bring ever in their season gifts from this garden.

poems.title: Book IX, 335
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The two statues, wayfarer, are the gift of the woodman Miccalion; but look, Hermes, how the excellent woodman from his wretched calling managed to give gifts. The good man is always good.

poems.title: Book IX, 337
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Good sport! thou who comest to the foot of this two-peaked hill, whether hunting the hare or in pursuit of winged game. Call on me, Pan the ranger of this forest, ‘from the rock, for I help both hounds and limed reeds to capture.

poems.title: Book IX, 563
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: If thou findest anywhere Democritus the lover of fruit, give him, Sir, this light message: that this is my season, the white-fruited fig-tree, and I bear for him the bread that wants no baking. Let him make haste, for my position is not secure, if he would pluck the fruit from my branches before they are stoned.

poems.title: Book IX, 719
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Myron did not mould me; he lied; but driving me from the herd where I was feeding, he fixed me to a stone base.

poems.title: Book IX, 744
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: The goatherds Soson and Simalus, rich in goats, stranger, seeing that they come from . . . dense with lentiscs, dedicated here to Hermes, the giver of cheeses and milk, this brazen, bearded goat, the lord of the flock.

poems.title: Book X, 1
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.note: Headed “Leonidas”; Paton’s Index of Authors gives Leonidas of Tarentum.
poems.text: It is the season for sailing ; already the chattering swallow has come, and the pleasant Zephyr, and the meadows bloom, and the sea with its boiling waves lashed by the rough winds has sunk to silence. Weigh the anchors and loose the hawsers, mariner, and sail with every stitch of canvas set. This, O man, I, Priapus, the god of the harbour, bid thee do that thou mayst sail for all kinds of merchandise.

poems.title: Book XVI, 182: On the Same
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Apelles having seen Cypris, the giver of marriage blessing, just escaped from her mother’s bosom and still wet with bubbling foam, figured her in her most delightsome loveliness, not painted, but alive. With beautiful grace doth she wring out her hair with her finger-tips, beautifully doth calm love flash from her eyes, and her paps, the heralds of her prime, are firm as quinces. Athena herself and the consort of Zeus shall say, “O Zeus, we are worsted in the judgment.”

poems.title: Book XVI, 190: On a Statue of Hermes
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Moricus the goatherd set me up, Hermes the overseer, to be the approved guardian of his fold. But, ye nannies who have taken your fill of green herbage on the mountains, heed not now at all the ravening wolf.

poems.title: Book XVI, 230
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Traveller, drink not here in the solitude this warm water so full of mud from the torrent, but go a little farther over this hill whereon the heifers are grazing, and by the shepherds’ pine there thou wilt find a fountain bubbling up through the generous rock, colder than the snow from the north.

poems.title: Book XVI, 236: On a Statue of Priapus
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: Here on the garden wall did Dinomenes set me up, wakeful Priapus, to guard his greens. But look, thief, how excited I am. And is this, you say, all for the sake of a few greens? For the sake of these few.

poems.title: Book XVI, 261: On Priapus
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text: I, Priapus, stand as a guardian at the meeting of the roads, my club standing straight out from my thighs. For Theocritus set me up to serve him faithfully. But keep your distance, Sir thief, lest you weep, receiving the thing you see.

poems.title: On the Same (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: May the seafarer have a prosperous voyage; but if, like me, the gale drive him into the harbour of Hades, let him blame not the inhospitable sea-gulf, but his own foolhardiness that loosed moorings from our tomb.

poems.title: On Prexo, Wife of Theocritus of Samos (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Who and of whom art thou, O woman, that liest under the Parian column? Prexo, daughter of Calliteles. And of what country? Of Samos. And also who buried thee? Theocritus, to whom my parents gave me in marriage. And of what diedst thou? Of child-birth. How old? Two-and-twenty. And childless? Nay, but I left a three-year-old Calliteles. May he live at least and come to great old age. And to thee, O stranger, may Fortune give all prosperity.

poems.title: Erinna (2) (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: The young maiden singer Erinna, the bee among poets, who sipped the flowers of the Muses, Hades snatched away to be his bride; truly indeed said the girl in her wisdom, "Thou art envious, O Death."

poems.title: The Hunter God (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Fair fall thy chase, O hunter of hares, and thou fowler who comest pursuing the winged people beneath this double hill; and cry thou to me, Pan, the guardian of the wood from my cliff; I join the chase with both dogs and reeds.

poems.title: Saved by Faith (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: They call me the little one, and say I cannot go straight and fearless on a prosperous voyage like ships that sail out to sea; and I deny it not; I am a little boat, but to the sea all is equal; fortune, not size, makes the difference. Let another have the advantage in rudders; for some put their confidence in this and some in that, but may my salvation be of God.

poems.title: The Roadside Pool (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Drink not here, traveller, from this warm pool in the brook, full of mud stirred by the sheep at pasture; but go a very little way over the ridge where the heifers are grazing; for there by yonder pastoral stone-pine thou wilt find bubbling through the fountained rock a spring colder than northern snow.

poems.title: Spring on the Coast (1) (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Now is the season of sailing; for already the chattering swallow is come, and the gracious west wind; the meadows flower, and the sea, tossed up with waves and rough blasts, has sunk to silence. Weigh thine anchors and unloose thine hawsers, O mariner, and sail with all thy canvas set: this I Priapus of the harbour bid thee, O man, that thou mayest sail forth to all thy trafficking.

poems.title: Sed Terrae Graviora (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Me, a hull that had measured such spaces of sea, fire consumed on the land that cut her pines to make me. Ocean brought me safe to shore; but I found her who bore me more treacherous than the sea.

poems.title: The Vintage-Revel (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: To the must-drinking Satyrs and to Bacchus, planter of the vine, Heronax consecrated the first handfuls of his plantation, these three casks from three vineyards, filled with the first flow of the wine; from which we, having poured such libation as is meet to crimson Bacchus and the Satyrs, will drink deeper than they.

poems.title: A Citizen of the Republic (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: A little dust of earth suffices me; let another lie richly, weighed down by his extravagant tombstone, that grim weight over the dead, who will know me here in death as Alcander son of Calliteles.

poems.title: The Withered Vine (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Even as a vine on her dry pole I support myself now on a staff, and death calls me to Hades. Be not obstinately deaf, O Gorgus; what is it the sweeter for thee if for three or four summers yet thou shalt warm thyself beneath the sun? So saying the aged man quietly put his life aside, and removed his house to the greater company.

poems.title: The Old Shepherd (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Shepherds who pass over this ridge of hill pasturing your goats and fleecy sheep, pay to Clitagoras, in Earth's name, a small but kindly grace, for the sake of Persephone under ground; let sheep bleat by me, and the shepherd on an unhewn stone pipe softly to them as they feed, and in early spring let the countryman pluck the meadow flower to engarland my tomb with a garland, and let one make milk drip from a fruitful ewe, holding up her milking-udder, to wet the base of my tomb: there are returns for favours to dead men, there are, even among the departed.

poems.title: The Little Sister (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: This girl passed to Hades untimely, in her seventh year, before her many playmates, poor thing, pining for her baby brother, who at twenty months old tasted of loveless Death. Alas, ill-fated Peristeris, how near at hand God has set the sorest griefs to men.

poems.title: Childless Among Women (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Ah wretched Anticles, and wretched I who have laid on the pyre in the flower of youth my only son, thee, child, who didst perish at eighteen years; and I weep, bewailing an orphaned old age: fain would I go to the shadowy house of Hades; neither is morn sweet to me, nor the beam of the swift sun. Ah wretched Anticles, struck down by fate, be thou healer of my sorrow, taking me with thee out of life.

poems.title: Two Eternities (Mackail)
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Infinite, O man, was the foretime until thou camest to thy dawn, and what remains is infinite on through Hades: what share is left for life but the bigness of a pinprick, and tinier than a pinprick if such there be? Little is thy life and afflicted; for not even so it is sweet, but more loathed than hateful death.

poems.title: Erinna
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
The lyric maid Erinna, the poet-bee that drew
The honey from the rarest blooms the muses' garden grew,
Hath Hades snatched to be his bride. Mark where the maiden saith,
Prophetic in her wisdom, 'How envious art thou, Death!'

poems.title: The Fountain Head
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Pause not here to drink thy fill
Where the sheep have stirred the rill,
And the pool lies warm and still--
Cross yon ridge a little way,
Where the grazing heifers stray,
And the stone-pine's branches sway
O'er a creviced rock below;
Thence the bubbling waters flow
Cooler than the northern snow.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.188: οὐκ ἀδικέω τὸν Ἔρωτα. γλυκύς
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
οὐκ ἀδικέω τὸν Ἔρωτα. γλυκύς, μαρτύρομαι αὐτὴν
Κύπριν βέβλημαι δʼ ἐκ δολίου κέραος,
καὶ πᾶς τεφροῦμαι· θερμὸν δʼ ἐπὶ θερμῷ ἰάλλει
ἄτρακτον, λωφᾷ δʼ οὐδʼ ὅσον ἰοβολῶν.
χὠ θνητὸς τὸν ἀλιτρὸν ἐγώ, κεἰ πτηνὸς ὁ δαίμων,
τίσομαι· ἐγκλήμων δʼ ἔσσομʼ ἀλεξόμενος;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca V.206: Μηλὼ καὶ Σατύρη τανυήλικες, Ἀντιγενείδεω
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Μηλὼ καὶ Σατύρη τανυήλικες, Ἀντιγενείδεω
παῖδες, ταὶ Μουσῶν εὔκολοι ἐργάτιδες·
Μηλὼ μὲν Μούσαις Πιμπληΐσι τοὺς ταχυχειλεῖς
αὐλοὺς καὶ ταύτην πύξινον αὐλοδόκην
ἡ φίλερως Σατύρη δὲ τὸν ἕσπερον οἰνοποτήρων
σύγκωμον, κηρῷ ζευξαμένη, δόνακα,
ἡδὺν συριστῆρα, σὺν ᾧ πανεπόρφνιος ἠῶ
ηὔγασεν αὐλείοις οὐ κοτέουσα θύραις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.4: Εὐκαπὲς ἄγκιστρον, καὶ δούρατα δουλιχόεντα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Εὐκαπὲς ἄγκιστρον, καὶ δούρατα δουλιχόεντα,
χὠρμιήν, καὶ τὰς ἰχθυδόκους σπυρίδας,
καὶ τοῦτον νηκτοῖσιν ἐπʼ ἰχθύσι τεχνασθέντα
κύρτον, ἁλιπλάγκτων εὕρεμα δικτυβόλων,
τρηχύν τε τριόδοντα, Ποσειδαώνιον ἔγχος,
καὶ τοὺς ἐξ ἀκάτων διχθαδίους ἐρέτας,
ὁ γριπεὺς Διόφαντος ἀνάκτορι θήκατο τέχνας,
ὡς θέμις, ἀρχαίας λείψανα τεχνοσύνας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.13: οἱ τρισσοί τοι ταῦτα τὰ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
οἱ τρισσοί τοι ταῦτα τὰ δίκτυα θῆκαν ὅμαιμοι,
ἀγρότα Πάν, ἄλλης ἄλλος ἀπʼ ἀγρεσίης·
ὧν ἀπὸ μὲν πτηνῶν Πίγρης τάδε, ταῦτα δὲ Δᾶμις
τετραπόδων, Κλείτωρ δʼ ὁ τρίτος εἰναλίων.
ἀνθʼ ὧν τῷ μὲν πέμπε διʼ ἠέρος εὔστοχον ἄγρην,
τῷ δὲ διὰ δρυμῶν, τῷ δὲ διʼ ἠϊόνων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.35: τοῦτο χιμαιροβάτᾳ Τελέσων αἰγώνυχι Πανὶ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τοῦτο χιμαιροβάτᾳ Τελέσων αἰγώνυχι Πανὶ
τὸ σκύλος ἀγρείας τεῖνε κατὰ πλατάνου·
καὶ τὰν ῥαιβόκρανον ἐυστόρθυγγα κορύναν,
ἃ πάρος αἱμωποὺς ἐστυφέλιξε λύκους,
γαυλούς τε γλαγοπῆγας, ἀγωγαῖόν τε κυνάγχαν,
καὶ τὰν εὐρίνων λαιμοπέδαν σκυλάκων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.44: Γλευκοπόταις Σατύροισι καὶ ἀμπελοφύτορι Βάκχῳ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Γλευκοπόταις Σατύροισι καὶ ἀμπελοφύτορι Βάκχῳ
Ἡρῶναξ πρώτης δράγματα φυταλιῆς,
τρισσῶν οἰνοπέδων τρισσοὺς ἱερώσατο τούσδε,
ἐμπλήσας οἴνου πρωτοχύτοιο, κάδους·
ὧν ἡμεῖς σπείσαντες, ὅσον θέμις, οἴνοπι Βάκχῳ
καὶ Σατύροις, Σατύρων πλείονα πιόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.120: οὐ μόνον ὑψηλοῖς ἐπὶ δένδρεσιν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
οὐ μόνον ὑψηλοῖς ἐπὶ δένδρεσιν οἶδα καθίζων
ἀείδειν, ζαθερεῖ καύματι θαλπόμενος,
προίκιος ἀνθρώποισι κελευθίτῃσιν ἀοιδός,
θηλείης ἔρσης ἰκμάδα γευόμενος·
ἀλλὰ καὶ εὐπήληκος Ἀθηναίης ἐπὶ δουρὶ
τὸν τέττιγʼ ὄψει μʼ, ὦνερ, ἐφεζόμενον.
ὅσσον γὰρ Μούσαις ἐστέργμεθα, τόσσον Ἀθήνη
ἐξ ἡμέων ἡ γὰρ παρθένος αὐλοθέτει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.129: ὀκτώ τοι θυρεούς, ὀκτὼ κράνη
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ὀκτώ τοι θυρεούς, ὀκτὼ κράνη, ὀκτὼ ὑφαντοὺς
θώρηκας, τόσσας θʼ αἱμαλέας κοπίδας,
ταῦτʼ ἀπὸ Λευκανῶν Κορυφασίᾳ ἔντεʼ Ἀθάνᾳ
Ἅγνων Εὐάνθευς θῆχʼ ὁ βιαιομάχας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.130: τοὺς θυρεοὺς ὁ Μολοσσὸς Ἰτωνίδι
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τοὺς θυρεοὺς ὁ Μολοσσὸς Ἰτωνίδι δῶρον Ἀθάνᾳ
Πύρρος ἀπὸ θρασέων ἐκρέμασεν Γαλατᾶν,
πάντα τὸν Ἀντιγόνου καθελὼν στρατὸν οὐ μέγα θαῦμα·
αἰχμηταὶ καὶ νῦν καὶ πάρος Αἰακίδαι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.131: αἵδʼ ἀπὸ Λευκανῶν θυρεάσπιδες, οἱ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
αἵδʼ ἀπὸ Λευκανῶν θυρεάσπιδες, οἱ δὲ χαλινοὶ
στοιχηδόν, ξεσταὶ τʼ ἀμφίβολοι κάμακες
δέδμηνται, ποθέουσαι ὁμῶς ἵππους τε καὶ ἄνδρας,
Παλλάδι· τοὺς δʼ ὁ μέλας ἀμφέχανεν θάνατος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.188: ὁ Κρὴς Θηρίμαχος τὰ λαγωβόλα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ὁ Κρὴς Θηρίμαχος τὰ λαγωβόλα Πανὶ Λυκαίῳ
ταῦτα πρὸς Ἀρκαδικοῖς ἐκρέμασε σκοπέλοις.
ἀλλὰ σὺ Θηριμάχῳ δώρων χάριν, ἀγρότα δαῖμον,
χεῖρα κατιθύνοις τοξότιν ἐν πολέμῳ,
ἔν τε συναγκείαισι παρίστασο δεξιτερῇ οἱ,
πρῶτα διδοὺς ἄγρης, πρῶτα καὶ ἀντιπάλων. .

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.200: ἐκ τόκου, Εἰλείθυια, πικρὰν ὠδῖνα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἐκ τόκου, Εἰλείθυια, πικρὰν ὠδῖνα φυγοῦσα,
ἀμβροσίη κλεινῶν θήκατό σοι πρὸ ποδῶν
δεσμὰ κόμας καὶ πέπλον, ἐφʼ ᾧ δεκάτῳ ἐνὶ μηνὶ
δισσὸν ἀπὸ ζώνης κῦμʼ ἐλόχευσε τέκνων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.202: Εὐθύσανον ζώνην τοι ὁμοῦ καὶ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Εὐθύσανον ζώνην τοι ὁμοῦ καὶ τόνδε κύπασσιν
Ἀτθὶς παρθενίων θῆκεν ὕπερθε θυρῶν,
ἐκ τόκου, ὦ Λητωΐ, βαρυνομένης ὅτε νηδὺν
ζωὸν ἀπʼ ὠδίνων λύσαο τῆσδε βρέφος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.204: Θῆρις ὁ δαιδαλόχειρ τᾷ Παλλάδι
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Θῆρις ὁ δαιδαλόχειρ τᾷ Παλλάδι πῆχυν ἀκαμπῆ,
καὶ τετανὸν νώτῳ καμπτόμενον πρίονα,
καὶ πέλεκυν ῥυκάναν τʼ εὐαυγέα, καὶ περιαγὲς
τρύπανον, ἐκ τέχνας ἄνθετο παυσάμενος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.205: τέκτονος ἄρμενα ταῦτα Λεοντίχου, αἵ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τέκτονος ἄρμενα ταῦτα Λεοντίχου, αἵ τε χαρακταὶ
ῥῖναι, καὶ κάλων οἱ ταχινοὶ βορέες,
στάθμαι καὶ μιλτεῖα, καὶ αἱ σχεδὸν ἀμφιπλῆγες
σφῦραι, καὶ μίλτῳ φυρόμενοι κανόνες,
αἳ τʼ ἀρίδες, ξυστήρ τε, καὶ ἐστελεωμένος οὗτος
ἐμβριθής, τέχνας ὁ πρύτανις, πέλεκυς,
τρύπανά τʼ εὐδίνητα, καὶ ὠκήεντα τέρετρα,
καὶ γόμφων οὗτοι τοὶ πίσυρες τορέες,
ἀμφίξουν τε σκέπαρνον· ἃ δὴ χαριεργῷ Ἀθάνᾳ
ὡνὴρ ἐκ τέχνας θήκατο παυόμενος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.211: τὸν ἀργυροῦν Ἔρωτα, καὶ περίσφυρον
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τὸν ἀργυροῦν Ἔρωτα, καὶ περίσφυρον
πέζαν, τὸ πορφυρεῦν τε Λεσβίδος κόμης
ἕλιγμα, καὶ μηλοῦχον ὑαλόχροα,
τὸ χάλκεὸν τʼ ἔσοπτρον, ἠδὲ τὸν πλατὺν
τριχῶν σαγηνευτῆρα, πύξινον κτένα,
ὧν ἤθελεν τυχοῦσα, γνησία Κύπρι,
ἐν σαῖς τίθησι Καλλίκλεια παστάσιν,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.221: χειμερίην διὰ νύκτα, χαλαζήεντά τε
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
χειμερίην διὰ νύκτα, χαλαζήεντά τε συρμὸν
καὶ νιφετὸν φεύγων καὶ κρυόεντα πάγον,
μουνολέων, καὶ δὴ κεκακωμένος ἀθρόα γυῖα,
ἦλθε φιλοκρήμνων αὖλιν ἐς αἰγινόμων.
οἱ δʼ οὐκ ἀμφʼ αἰγῶν μεμελημένοι, ἀλλὰ περὶ σφέων,
εἵατο σωτῆρα Ζῆνʼ ἐπικεκλόμενοι.
χεῖμα δὲ θὴρ μείνας, θὴρ νύκτιος, οὔτε τινʼ ἀνδρῶν
οὔτε βοτῶν βλάψας, ᾠχετʼ ἀπαυλόσυνος.
οἱ δὲ πάθης ἔργον τόδʼ ἐϋγραφὲς ἀκρολοφίτᾳ
Πανὶ παρʼ εὐπρέμνῳ τᾷδʼ ἀνέθεντο δρυΐ;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.226: τοῦτʼ ὀλίγον Κλείτωνος ἐπαύλιον, ἥ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τοῦτʼ ὀλίγον Κλείτωνος ἐπαύλιον, ἥ τʼ ὀλιγῶλαξ
σπείρεσθαι, λιτός θʼ ὁ σχεδὸν ἀμπελεὼν,
τοῦτό τε ῥωπεῖον ὀλιγόξυλον ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ τούτοις
Κλείτων ὀγδώκοντʼ ἐξεπέρησ’ ἔτεα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.262: τὸν ποίμνην καὶ ἔπαυλα βοῶν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τὸν ποίμνην καὶ ἔπαυλα βοῶν καὶ βώτορας ἄνδρας
σινόμενον, κλαγγὰν τʼ οὐχὶ τρέσαντα κυνῶν,
Εὐάλκης ὁ Κρὴς ἐπινύκτια μῆλα νομεύων
πέφνε, καὶ ἐκ ταύτης ἐκρέμασεν πίτυος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.263: Πυρσῶ τοῦτο λέοντος ἀπʼ ὦν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Πυρσῶ τοῦτο λέοντος ἀπʼ ὦν φλοιώσατο δέρμα
Σῶσος ὁ βουπάμων, δουρὶ φονευσάμενος,
ἄρτι καταβρύκοντα τὸν εὐθηλήμονα μόσχον,
οὐδʼ ἵκετʼ ἐκ μάνδρας αὖθις ἐπὶ ξύλοχον
μοσχείω δʼ ἀπέτισεν ὁ θὴρ ἀνθʼ αἵματος αἷμα,
βληθείς· ἀχθεινὰν δʼ εἶδε βοοκτασίαν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.281: Δίνδυμα καὶ Φρυγίης πυρικαέος ἀμφιπολεῦσα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Δίνδυμα καὶ Φρυγίης πυρικαέος ἀμφιπολεῦσα
πρῶνας, τὴν μικρήν, Μῆτερ, Ἀριστοδίκην,
κούρην Σειλήνης, παμπότνια, κεἰς ὑμέναιον
κεἰς γάμον ἁδρύναις, πείρατα κουροσύνας·
ἀνθʼ ὧν σοι κατὰ πολλὰ προνήια καὶ παρὰ βωμῷ
παρθενικὴν ἐτίναξʼ ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα κόμην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.286: τῆς πέζης τὰ μὲν ἄκρα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τῆς πέζης τὰ μὲν ἄκρα τὰ δεξιὰ μέχρι παλαιστῆς
καὶ σπιθαμῆς οὔλης Βίττιον εἰργάσατο·
θάτερα δʼ Ἀντιάνειρα προσήρμοσε· τὸν δὲ μεταξὺ
Μαίανδρον καὶ τὰς παρθενικὰς Βιτίη.
κουρᾶν καλλίστη Διός, Ἄρτεμι, τοῦτο τὸ νῆμα
πρὸς ψυχῆς θείης, τὴν τριπόνητον ἔριν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.288: αἱ Λυκομήδευς παῖδες, Ἀθηνὼ καὶ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
αἱ Λυκομήδευς παῖδες, Ἀθηνὼ καὶ Μελίτεια
καὶ Φιντὼ Γληνὶς θʼ, αἱ φιλοεργόταται,
ἔργων ἐκ δεκάτας ποτιθύμια, τόν τε πρόσεργον
ἄτρακτον, καὶ τὰν ἄτρια κριναμέναν
κερκίδα, τὰν ἱστῶν μολπάτιδα, καὶ τὰ τροχαῖα
πανία, κερταστὰς τούσδε ποτιρρογέας,
καὶ σπάθας εὐβριθεῖς πολυάργυρα· τὼς δὲ πενιχραὶ
ἐξ ὀλίγων ὀλίγην μοῖραν ἀπαρχόμεθα,
τῶν χέρας αἰέν, Ἀθάνα, ἐπιπλήσαις μὲν ὀπίσσω,
θείης δʼ εὐσιπύους ἐξ ὀλιγησιπύων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.289: Αὐτονόμα, Μελίτεια, Βοΐσκιον, αἱ Φιλολᾴδεω
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Αὐτονόμα, Μελίτεια, Βοΐσκιον, αἱ Φιλολᾴδεω
καὶ Νικοῦς Κρῆσσαι τρεῖς, ξένε, θυγατέρες,
ἁ μὲν τὸν μιτόεργον ἀειδίνητον ἄτρακτον,
ἁ δὲ τὸν ὀρφνίταν εἰροκόμον τάλαρον,
ἁ δʼ ἅμα τὰν πέπλων εὐάτριον ἐργάτιν, ἱστῶν
κερκίδα, τὰν λεχέων Πανελόπας φύλακα,
δῶρον Ἀθαναίᾳ Πανίτιδι τῷδʼ ἐνὶ ναῷ
θῆκαν, Ἀθαναίας παυσάμεναι καμάτων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.293: ὁ σκήπων καὶ ταῦτα τὰ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ὁ σκήπων καὶ ταῦτα τὰ βλαυτία, πότνια Κύπρι,
ἄγκειται κυνικοῦ σκῦλʼ ἀπὸ Σωχάρεος,
ὄλπη τε ῥυπόεσσα, πολυτρήτοιό τε πήρας
λείψανον, ἀρχαίης πληθόμενον σοφίης·
σοὶ δὲ Ῥόδων ὁ καλός, τὸν πάνσοφον ἡνίκα πρέσβυν
ἤγρευσεν, στεπτοῖς θήκατʼ ἐπὶ προθύροις,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.296: Ἀστεμφῆ ποδάγρην, καὶ δούνακας ἀνδικτῆρας
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Ἀστεμφῆ ποδάγρην, καὶ δούνακας ἀνδικτῆρας,
καὶ λίνα, καὶ γυρὸν τοῦτο λαγωοβόλον,
ἰοδόκην, καὶ τοῦτον ἐπʼ ὄρτυγι τετρανθέντα
αὐλὸν, καὶ πλωτῶν εὐπλεκὲς ἀμφίβολον,
Ἑρμείῃ Σώσιππος, ἐπεὶ παρενήξατο τὸ πλεῦν
ἥβης, ἐκ γήρως δʼ ἀδρανίῃ δέδεται.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.298: πήρην, κάδέψητον ἀπεσκληρυμμένον αἰγὸς
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
πήρην, κάδέψητον ἀπεσκληρυμμένον αἰγὸς
στέρφος, καὶ βάκτρον τοῦτὸ γʼ ὁδοιπορικόν,
κὤλπαν ἀστλέγγιστον, ἀχάλκωτόν τε κυνοῦχον,
καὶ πῖλον κεφαλᾶς οὐχ ὁσίας σκέπανον
ταῦτα καταφθιμένοιο μυρικίνεον περὶ θάμνον
σκῦλʼ ἀπὸ Σωχάρεος Λιμὸς ἀνεκρέμασεν,

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.300: Λαθρίη, ἐκ πλανίου ταύτην χάριν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Λαθρίη, ἐκ πλανίου ταύτην χάριν ἔκ τε πενέστεω
κἠξ ὀλιγησιπύου δέξο Λεωνίδεω,
ψαιστά τε πιήεντα καὶ εὐθήσαυρον ἐλαίην,
καὶ τοῦτο χλωρὸν σῦκον ἀποκράδιον,
κεὐοίνου σταφυλῆς ἔχʼ ἀποσπάδα πεντάρραγον,
πότνια, καὶ σπονδὴν τήνδʼ ὑποπυθμίδιον.
ἢν δὲ μέ γʼ, ὡς ἐκ νούσου ἀνειρύσω, ὧδε καὶ ἐχθρῆς
ἐκ πενίης ῥύσῃ, δέξο χιμαιροθύτην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.302: Φεύγεθʼ ὑπὲκ καλύβης, σκότιοι μύες
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Φεύγεθʼ ὑπὲκ καλύβης, σκότιοι μύες· οὔτι πενιχρὴ
μῦς σιπύη βόσκειν οἶδε Λεωνίδεω.
αὐτάρκης ὁ πρέσβυς ἔχων ἅλα καὶ δύο κρῖμνα·
ἐκ πατέρων ταύτην ᾐνέσαμεν βιοτήν.
τῷ τί μεταλλεύεις τοῦτον μυχόν, ὦ φιλόλιχνε,
οὐδʼ ἀποδειπνιδίου γευόμενος σκυβάλου;
σπεύδων εἰς ἄλλους οἴκους ἴθι τἀμὰ δὲ λιτἄ,
ὧν ἄπο πλειοτέρην οἴσεαι ἁρμαλιήν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.305: Λαβροσύνᾳ τάδε δῶρα φιλευχύλῳ τε
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Λαβροσύνᾳ τάδε δῶρα φιλευχύλῳ τε Λαφυγμῷ
θήκατο δεισόζου Δωριέος κεφαλά·
τὼς Λαρισσαίως βουγάστορας ἑψητῆρας,
καὶ χύτρως, καὶ τὰν εὐρυχαδῆ κύλικα,
καὶ τὰν εὐχάλκωτον ἐύγναμπτόν τε κρεάγραν,
καὶ κνῆστιν, καὶ τὰν ἐτνοδόνον τορύναν.
Λαβροσύνα;, σὺ δὲ ταῦτα κακοῦ κακὰ δωρητῆρος
δεξαμένα, νεύσαις μή ποκα σωφροσύναν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.309: εὔφημόν τοι σφαῖραν, ἐυκρόταλόν τε
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
εὔφημόν τοι σφαῖραν, ἐυκρόταλόν τε Φιλοκλῆς
Ἑρμείῃ ταύτην πυξινέην πλατάγην,
ἀστραγάλας θʼ αἷς πόλλʼ ἐπεμήνατο, καὶ τὸν ἑλικτὸν
ῥόμβον, κουροσύνης παίγνιʼ ἀνεκρέμασεν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.334: αὔλια καὶ Νυμφέων ἱερὸς πάγος
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
αὔλια καὶ Νυμφέων ἱερὸς πάγος, αἳ θʼ ὑπὸ πέτρῃ
πίδακες, ἥ θʼ ὕδασιν γειτονέουσα πίτυς,
καὶ σὺ τετραγλώχιν, μηλοσσόε, Μαιάδος Ἑρμᾶ,
ὅς τε τὸν αἰγιβότην, Πάν, κατέχεις σκόπελον,
ἵλαοι τὰ ψαιστὰ τό τε σκύφος ἔμπλεον οἴνης
δέξασθʼ, Αἰακίδεω δῶρα Νεοπτολέμου.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.355: ἁ μάτηρ ζῷον τὸν Μίκυθον
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἁ μάτηρ ζῷον τὸν Μίκυθον, οἷα πενιχρὰ
Βάκχῳ δωρεῖται, ῥωπικὰ γραψαμένα.
Βάκχε, σὺ δʼ ὑψῴης τὸν Μίκυθον εἰ δὲ τὸ δῶρον
ῥωπικόν, ἁ λιτὰ ταῦτα φέρει πενία.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.163: α. τίς τίνος εὖσα, γύναι
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
α. τίς τίνος εὖσα, γύναι, Παρίην ὑπὸ κίονα κεῖσαι;
β. Πρηξὼ Καλλιτέλευς. α. καὶ ποδαπή; β. Σαμίη.
α. τίς δέ σε καὶ κτερέιξε; β. Θεόκριτος, ᾧ με γονῆες
ἐξέδοσαν. α. θνῄσκεις δʼ ἐκ τίνος ; β. ἐκ τοκετοῦ.
α. εὖσα πόσων ἐτέων ; β. δύο κεἴκοσιν. α. ἦ ῥὰ γʼ ἄτεκνος ;
β. οὔκ, ἀλλὰ τριετῆ Καλλιτέλην ἔλιπον.
α. Ζώοι σοι κεῖνός γε, καὶ ἐς βαθὺ γῆρας ἵκοιτο.
β. καὶ σοί, ξεῖνε, πόροι πάντα Τύχη τὰ καλά.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.198: εἰ καὶ μικρὸς ἰδεῖν καὶ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
εἰ καὶ μικρὸς ἰδεῖν καὶ ἐπʼ οὔδεος, ὦ παροδῖτα,
λᾶας ὁ τυμβίτης ἄμμιν ἐπικρέμαται,
αἰνοίης, ὤνθρωπε, Φιλαινίδα· τὴν γὰρ ἀοιδὸν
ἀκρίδα, τὴν εὖσαν τὸ πρὶν ἀκανθοβάτιν,
διπλοῦς ἐς λυκάβαντας ἐφίλατο τὴν καλαμῖτιν,
κἀμφίεφʼ ὑμνιδίῳ χρησαμένην πατάγῳ·
καὶ μʼ οὐδὲ φθιμένην ἀπανήνατο· τοῦτο δʼ ἐφʼ ἡμῖν
τὠλίγον ὤρθωσεν σᾶμα πολυστροφίης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.264: εἴη ποντοπόρῳ πλόος οὔριος· ὃν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
εἴη ποντοπόρῳ πλόος οὔριος· ὃν δʼ ἄρʼ ἀήτης,
ὡς ἐμέ, τοῖς Ἀίδεω· προσπελάσῃ λιμέσιν,
μεμφέσθω μὴ λαῖτμα κακόξενον, ἀλλʼ ἕο τόλμαν,
ὅστις ἀφʼ ἡμετέρου πείσματʼ ἔλυσε τάφου.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.266: Ναυηγοῦ τάφος εἰμὶ Διοκλέος· οἱ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Ναυηγοῦ τάφος εἰμὶ Διοκλέος· οἱ δʼ ἀνάγονται,
φεῦ τόλμης, ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ πείσματα λυσάμενοι.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.273: Εὔρου με τρηχεῖα καὶ αἰπήεσσα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Εὔρου με τρηχεῖα καὶ αἰπήεσσα καταιγίς,
καὶ νύξ, καὶ δνοφερῆς κύματα πανδυσίης
ἔβλαψʼ Ὠρίωνος· ἀπώλισθον δὲ βίοιο
Κάλλαισχρος, Λιβυκοῦ μέσσα θέων πελάγευς.
κἀγὼ μὲν πόντῳ δινεύμενος, ἰχθύσι κύρμα,
οἴχημαι· ψεύστης δʼ οὗτος ἔπεστι λίθος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.283: τετρηχυῖα θάλασσα, τί μʼ οὐκ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τετρηχυῖα θάλασσα, τί μʼ οὐκ οἰζυρὰ παθόντα
τηλόσ’ ἀπὸ ψιλῆς ἔπτυσας ἠιόνος;
ὡς σεῦ μηδʼ Ἀίδαο κακὴν ἐπιειμένος ἀχλὺν
Φυλεὺς Ἀμφιμένευς ἆσσον ἐγειτόνεον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.295: Θῆριν τὸν τριγέροντα, τὸν εὐάγρων
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Θῆριν τὸν τριγέροντα, τὸν εὐάγρων ἀπὸ κύρτων
ζῶντα, τὸν αἰθυίης πλείονα νηξάμενον,
ἰχθυσιληϊστῆρα, σαγηνέα, χηραμοδύτην,
οὐχὶ πολυσκάλμου πλώτορα ναυτιλίης,
ἔμπης οὔτʼ Ἀρκτοῦρος ἀπώλεσεν, οὔτε καταιγὶς
ἤλασε τὰς πολλὰς τῶν ἐτέων δεκάδας·
ἀλλʼ ἔθανʼ ἐν καλύβῃ σχοινίτιδι, λύχνος ὁποῖα,
τῷ μακρῷ σβεσθεὶς ἐν χρόνῳ αὐτόματος.
σῆμα δὲ τοῦτʼ οὐ παῖδες ἐφήρμοσαν, οὐδʼ ὁμόλεκτρος,
ἀλλὰ συνεργατίνης ἰχθυβόλων θίασος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.316: τὴν ἐπʼ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τὴν ἐπʼ
ἐμεῦ στήλην παραμείβεο, μήτε με χαίρειν
εἰπὼν, μήθʼ
ὅστις, μὴ τίνος ἐξετάσας·
ἢ μὴ τὴν ἀνύεις τελέσαις ὁδὸν ἢν δὲ παρέλθῃς
σιγῇ, μηδʼ οὕτως ἣν ἀνύεις τελέσαις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.408: ἀτρέμα τὸν τύμβον παραμείβετε, μὴ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἀτρέμα τὸν τύμβον παραμείβετε, μὴ τὸν ἐν ὕπνῳ
πικρὸν ἐγείρητε σφῆκʼ ἀναπαυόμενον.
ἄρτι γὰρ Ἱππώνακτος ὁ καὶ τοκεῶνε βαΰξας
ἄρτι κεκοίμηται θυμὸς ἐν ἡσυχίῃ.
ἀλλὰ προμηθήσασθε· τὰ γὰρ πεπυρωμένα κείνου
ῥήματα πημαίνειν οἶδε καὶ εἰν Ἀίδῃ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.422: τί στοχασώμεθά σου, Πεισίστρατε, χῖον
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.440: ἠρίον, οἷον νυκτὶ καταφθιμένοιο καλύπτεις
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἠρίον, οἷον νυκτὶ καταφθιμένοιο καλύπτεις
ὀστέον, οἵην, γαῖʼ, ἀμφέχανες κεφαλήν,
πολλὸν μὲν ξανθαῖσιν ἀρεσκομένου Χαρίτεσσι,
πολλοῦ δʼ ἐν μνήμῃ πᾶσιν Ἀριστοκράτης.
ᾔδει Ἀριστοκράτης καὶ μείλιχα δημολογῆσαι,
[ στρεβλὴν οὐκ ὀφρὺν ἐσθλὸς ἐφελκόμενος·
ᾔδει καὶ Βάκχοιο παρὰ κρητῆρος ἄδηριν]
ἰθῦναι κείνην εὐκύλικα λαλιὴν
ᾔδει καὶ ξείνοισι καὶ ἐνδήμοισι προσηνέα
ἔρδειν. γαῖʼ ἐρατή, τοῖον ἔχεις φθίμενον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.448: Πραταλίδα τὸ μνᾶμα Λυκαστίω, ἄκρον
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Πραταλίδα τὸ μνᾶμα Λυκαστίω, ἄκρον ἐρώτων
εἰδότος, ἄκρα μάχας, ἄκρα λινοστασίας,
ἄκρα χοροιτυπίας. χθόνιοι, Μίνωϊ τὸν ἄνδρα
τοῦτον, Κρηταιεῖς Κρῆτα, παρῳκίσατε.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.452: Μεμνησθʼ Εὐβούλοιο σαόφρονος, ὦ παριόντες
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Μεμνησθʼ Εὐβούλοιο σαόφρονος, ὦ παριόντες.
πίνωμεν κοινὸς πᾶσι λιμὴν Ἀίδης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.455: Μαρωνὶς ἡ φίλοινος, ἡ πίθων
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Μαρωνὶς ἡ φίλοινος, ἡ πίθων σποδός,
ἐνταῦθα κεῖται γρῆϋς, ἧς ὑπὲρ τάφου
γνωστὸν πρόκειται πᾶσιν Ἀττικὴ κύλιξ.
στένει δὲ καὶ γᾶς νέρθεν, οὐχ ὑπὲρ τέκνων,
οὐδʼ ἀνδρός, οὓς λέλοιπεν ἐνδεεῖς βίου·
ἓν δʼ ἀντὶ πάντων, οὕνεχʼ ἡ κύλιξ κενή.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.463: αὕτα Τιμόκλειʼ, αὕτα Φιλώ, αὕτα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
αὕτα Τιμόκλειʼ, αὕτα Φιλώ, αὕτα Ἀριστώ,
αὕτα Τιμαιθώ, παῖδες Ἀριστοδίκου,
πᾶσαι ὑπʼ ὠδῖνος πεφονευμέναι· αἷς ἔπι τοῦτο
σᾶμα πατὴρ στάσας κάτθανʼ Ἀριστόδικος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.466: ἆ δείλʼ Ἀντίκλεις, δειλὴ δʼ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἆ δείλʼ Ἀντίκλεις, δειλὴ δʼ ἐγὼ ἡ τὸν ἐν ἥβης
ἀκμῇ καὶ μοῦνον παῖδα πυρωσαμένη,
ὀκτωκαιδεκέτης ὃς ἀπώλεο, τέκνον ἐγὼ δʼ
ὀρφάνιον κλαίω γῆρας ὀδυρομένη.
βαίην εἰς Ἄϊδος σκιερὸν δόμον οὔτε μοι ἠὼς
ἡδεῖʼ οὔτʼ ἀκτὶς ὠκέος ἠελίου.
ἆ δείλʼ Ἀντίκλεις, μεμορημένε, πένθεος εἴης
ἰητήρ, ζωῆς ἔκ με κομισσάμενος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.472: μυρίος ἦν, ἄνθρωπε, χρόνος προτοῦ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
μυρίος ἦν, ἄνθρωπε, χρόνος προτοῦ, ἄχρι πρὸς ἠῶ
ἦλθες, χὠ λοιπὸς μυρίος εἰς ἀίδην.
τίς μοῖρα ζωῆς ὑπολείπεται, ἢ ὅσον ὅσσον
στιγμὴ καὶ στιγμῆς εἴ τι χαμηλότερον;
μικρή σευ ζωὴ τεθλιμμένη· οὐδὲ γὰρ αὐτὴ
ἡδεῖʼ, ἀλλʼ ἐχθροῦ στυγνοτέρη θανάτου.
ἐκ τοίης ὥνθρωποι ἀπηκριβωμένοι ὀστῶν
ἁρμονίης, ὕψιστʼ ἠέρα καὶ νεφέλας·
ὦνερ, ἴδʼ ὡς ἀχρεῖον, ἐπεὶ περὶ νήματος ἄκρον
εὐλὴ ἀκέρκιστον λῶπος ἐφεζομένη·
οἷον τὸ ψαλα, θρῖον ἀπεψιλωμένον οἷον,
πόλλον ἀραχναίου στυγνότερον σκελετοῦ.
ἠοῦν ἐξ ἠοῦς ὅσσον σθένος, ὦνερ, ἐρευνῶν
εἴης ἐν λιτῇ κεκλιμένος βιοτῇ·
αἰὲν τοῦτο νόῳ μεμνημένος ἄχρις ὁμιλῇς
ζωοῖς, ἐξ οἵης ἡρμόνισαι καλάμης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.472b: χειμέριον ζωὴν ὑπαλεύεο, νεῖο δʼ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
χειμέριον ζωὴν ὑπαλεύεο, νεῖο δʼ ἐς ὅρμον,
ὡς κἠγὼ Φείδων ὁ Κρίτου εἰς ἀίδην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.478: τίς ποτʼ ἄρʼ εἶ; τίνος
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τίς ποτʼ ἄρʼ εἶ; τίνος ἆρα παρὰ τρίβον ὀστέα ταῦτα
τλήμονʼ ἐν ἡμιφαεῖ λάμνακι γυμνὰ μένει;
μνῆμα δὲ καὶ τάφος αἰὲν ἀμαξεύοντος ὁδίτεω
ἄξονι καὶ τροχιᾖ λιτὰ παραξέεται·
ἤδη σου καὶ πλευρὰ παρατρίψουσιν ἄμαξαι,
σχέτλιε, σοὶ δʼ οὐδεὶς οὐδʼ ἐπὶ δάκρυ βαλεῖ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.480: ἤδη μευ τέτριπται ὑπεκκεκαλυμμένον ὀστεῦν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἤδη μευ τέτριπται ὑπεκκεκαλυμμένον ὀστεῦν
ἁρμονίᾐ τʼ, ὦνερ, πλὰξ ἐπικεκλιμένη·
ἤδη καὶ σκώληκες ὑπὲκ σοροῦ αὐγάζονται
ἡμετέρης· τί πλέον γῆν ἐπιεννύμεθα;
ἦ γὰρ τὴν οὔπω πρὶν ἰτὴν ὁδὸν ἐτμήξαντο
ἄνθρωποι, κατʼ ἐμῆς νισσόμενοι κεφαλῆς.
ἀλλὰ πρὸς ἐγγαίων, Ἀϊδωνέος Ἑρμεία τε
καὶ Νυκτός, ταύτης ἐκτὸς ἴτʼ ἀτραπιτοῦ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.503: α. ἀρχαίης ὦ θινὸς ἐπεστηλωμένον
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
α. ἀρχαίης ὦ θινὸς ἐπεστηλωμένον ἄχθος,
εἴποις ὅντινʼ ἔχεις, ἢ τίνος, ἢ ποδαπόν.
β. Φίντωνʼ Ἑρμιονῆα Βαθυκλέος, ὃν πολὺ κῦμα
ὤλεσεν, Ἀρκτούρου λαίλαπι χρησάμενον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.504: Πάρμις ὁ Καλλιγνώτου ἐπακταῖος καλαμευτής
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Πάρμις ὁ Καλλιγνώτου ἐπακταῖος καλαμευτής,
ἄκρος καὶ κίχλης καὶ σκάρου ἰχθυβολεύς,
καὶ λάβρου πέρκης δελεάρπαγος, ὅσσα τε κοίλας
σήραγγας πέτρας τʼ ἐμβυθίους νέμεται,
ἄγρης ἐκ πρώτης ποτʼ ἰουλίδα πετρήεσσαν
δακνάζων, ὀλοὴν ἐξ ἁλὸς ἀράμενος,
ἔφθιτʼ ὀλισθηρὴ γὰρ ὑπʼ ἐκ χερὸς ἀίξασα
ᾤχετʼ ἐπὶ στεινὸν παλλομένη φάρυγα.
χὠ μὲν μηρίνθων καὶ δούνακος ἀγκίστρων τε
ἐγγὺς ἀπὸ πνοιὴν ἧκε κυλινδόμενος,
νήματʼ ἀναπλήσας ἐπιμοίρια· τοῦ δὲ θανόντος
Γρίπων ὁ γριπεὺς τοῦτον ἔχωσε τάφον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.506: κἠν γῇ καὶ πόντῳ κεκρύμμεθα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
κἠν γῇ καὶ πόντῳ κεκρύμμεθα· τοῦτο περισσὸν
ἐκ Μοιρέων Θάρσυς Χαρμίδου ἠνύσατο.
ἦ γὰρ ἐπʼ ἀγκύρης ἔνοχον βάρος εἰς ἅλα δύνων,
Ἰόνιὸν θʼ ὑγρὸν κῦμα κατερχόμενος,
τὴν μὲν ἔσωσ’, αὐτὸς δὲ μετάτροπος ἐκ βυθοῦ ἔρρων
ἤδη καὶ ναύταις χεῖρας ὀρεγνύμενος,
ἐβρώθην τοῖόν μοι ἐπʼ ἄγριον εὖ μέγα κῆτος
ἦλθεν, ἀπέβροξεν δʼ ἄχρις ἐπʼ ὀμφαλίου.
χἤμισυ μὲν ναῦται, ψυχρὸν βάρος, ἐξ ἁλὸς ἡμῶν
ἤρανθʼ, ἥμισυ δὲ πρίστις ἀπεκλάσατο·
ᾐόνι δʼ ἐν ταύτῃ κακὰ λείψανα Θάρσυος, ὦνερ,
ἔκρυψαν πάτρην δʼ οὐ πάλιν ἱκόμεθα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.648: ἐσθλὸς Ἀριστοκράτης ὅτʼ ἀπέπλεεν εἰς
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἐσθλὸς Ἀριστοκράτης ὅτʼ ἀπέπλεεν εἰς Ἀχέροντα,
εἶπʼ ὀλιγοχρονίης ἁψάμενος κεφαλῆς·
“ παίδων τις μνήσαιτο, καὶ ἑδνώσαιτο γυναῖκα,
εἰ καί μιν δάκνοι δυσβίοτος πενίη·
ζωὴν στυλώσαιτο· κακὸς δʼ ἄστυλος ἰδέσθαι
οἶκος· ὃ δʼ αὖ λῷστον, τἀνέρος ἐσχαρεὼν
εὐκίων φαίνοιτο, καὶ ἐν πολυκαέι ὄγκῳ
ἐμπρέποι, αὐγάζων δαλὸν ἐπεσχάριον”
ᾔδει Ἀριστοκράτης τὸ κρήγυον ἀλλὰ γυναικῶν,
ὤνθρωπʼ, ἤχθαιρεν τὴν ἀλιτοφροσύνην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.652: ἠχήεσσα θάλασσα, τί τὸν Τιμάρεος
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἠχήεσσα θάλασσα, τί τὸν Τιμάρεος οὕτως
πλώοντʼ οὐ πολλῇ νηὶ Τελευταγόρην,
ἄγρια χειμήνασα, κατεπρηνώσαο πόντῳ
σὺν φόρτῳ, λάβρον κῦμʼ ἐπιχευαμένη;
χὠ μέν που καύηξιν ἢ ἰχθυβόροις λαρίδεσσιν
τεθρήνητʼ ἄπνους εὐρεῖ ἐπʼ αἰγιαλῷ·
Τιμάρης δὲ κενὸν τέκνου κεκλαυμένον ἀθρῶν
τύμβον, δακρύει παῖδα Τελευταγόρην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.654: αἰεὶ ληισταὶ καὶ ἁλιφθόροι, οὐδὲ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
αἰεὶ ληισταὶ καὶ ἁλιφθόροι, οὐδὲ δίκαιοι
Κρῆτες· τίς Κρητῶν οἶδε δικαιοσύνην;
ὡς καὶ ἐμὲ πλώοντα σὺν οὐκ εὐπίονι φόρτῳ
Κρηταιεῖς ὦσαν Τιμόλυτον καθʼ ἁλός,
δείλαιον. κἠγὼ μὲν ἁλιζώοις λαρίδεσσι
κέκλαυμαι, τύμβῳ δʼ οὐχ ὕπο Τιμόλυτος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.655: ἀρκεῖ μοι γαίης μικρὴ κόνις
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἀρκεῖ μοι γαίης μικρὴ κόνις· ἡ δὲ περισσὴ
ἄλλον ἐπιθλίβοι πλούσια κεκλιμένον
στήλη, τὸ σκληρὸν νεκρῶν βάρος· εἴ με θανόντα
γνώσοντʼ, Ἀλκάνδρῳ τοῦτο τί Καλλιτέλευς;

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.656: τὴν ὀλίγην βῶλον καὶ τοῦτʼ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τὴν ὀλίγην βῶλον καὶ τοῦτʼ ὀλιγήριον, ὦνερ,
σῆμα ποτίφθεγξαι τλάμονος Ἀλκιμένευς,
εἰ καὶ πᾶν κέκρυπται ὑπʼ ὀξείης παλιούρου
καὶ βάτου, ἥν ποτʼ ἐγὼ δήϊον Ἀλκιμένης.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.657: ποιμένες οἳ ταύτην ὄρεος ῥάχιν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ποιμένες οἳ ταύτην ὄρεος ῥάχιν οἰοπολεῖτε
αἶγας κεὐείρους ἐμβοτέοντες ὄις,
Κλειταγόρῃ, πρὸς Γῆς, ὀλίγην χάριν, ἀλλὰ προσηνῆ
τίνοιτε, χθονίης εἵνεκα Φερσεφόνης.
βληχήσαιντʼ ὄιές μοι, ἐπʼ ἀξέστοιο δὲ ποιμὴν
πέτρης συρίζοι πρηέα βοσκομέναις·
εἴαρι δὲ πρώτῳ λειμώνιον ἄνθος ἀμέρσας
χωρίτης στεφέτω τύμβον ἐμὸν στεφάνῳ,
καί τις ἀπʼ εὐάρνοιο καταχραίνοιτο γάλακτι
οἰός, ἀμολγαῖον μαστὸν ἀνασχόμενος,
κρηπῖδʼ ὑγραίνων ἐπιτύμβιον εἰσὶ θανόντων
εἰσὶν ἀμοιβαῖαι κἀν φθιμένοις χάριτες.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.665: μήτε μακρῇ θαρσέων ναυτίλλεο μήτε
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
μήτε μακρῇ θαρσέων ναυτίλλεο μήτε βαθείῃ
νηί· κρατεῖ παντὸς δούρατος εἷς ἄνεμος.
ὤλεσε καὶ Πρόμαχον πνοιὴ μία, κῦμα δʼ ἓν αὔτως
ἀθρόον ἐς κοίλην ἐστυφέλιξεν ἅλα.
οὐ μὴν οἱ δαίμων πάντῃ κακός· ἀλλʼ ἐνὶ γαίῃ
πατρίδι καὶ τύμβου καὶ κτερέων ἔλαχεν
κηδεμόνων ἐν χερσίν, ἐπεὶ τρηχεῖα θάλασσα
νεκρὸν πεπταμένους θῆκεν ἐπʼ αἰγιαλούς.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.715: πολλὸν ἀπʼ Ἰταλίης κεῖμαι χθονός
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
πολλὸν ἀπʼ Ἰταλίης κεῖμαι χθονός, ἔκ τε Τάραντος
πάτρης· τοῦτο δέ μοι πικρότερον θανάτου.
τοιοῦτος πλανίων ἄβιος βίος· ἀλλά με Μοῦσαι
ἔστερξαν, λυγρῶν δʼ ἀντὶ μελιχρὸν ἔχω.
οὔνομα δʼ οὐκ ἤμυσε Λεωνίδου· αὐτά με δῶρα
κηρύσσει Μουσέων πάντας ἐπʼ ἠελίους.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.719: Τέλληνος ὅδε τύμβος· ἔχω δʼ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Τέλληνος ὅδε τύμβος· ἔχω δʼ ὑποβωλέα πρέσβυν
τῆνον τὸν πρᾶτον γνόντα γελοιομελεῖν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.726: ἑσπέριον κἠῷον ἀπώσατο πολλάκις ὕπνον
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἑσπέριον κἠῷον ἀπώσατο πολλάκις ὕπνον
ἡ γρηῢς πενίην Πλατθὶς ἀμυνομένη·
καί τι πρὸς ἠλακάτην καὶ τὸν συνέριθον ἄτρακτον
ἤεισεν, πολιοῦ γήραος ἀγχίθυρος,
κἄτι παριστίδιος δινευμένη ἄχρις ἐπʼ ἠοῦς
κεῖνον Ἀθηναίης σὺν Χάρισιν δόλιχον,
ἢ ῥικνῇ ῥικνοῦ περὶ γούνατος ἄρκιον ἱστῷ
χειρὶ στρογγύλλουσ’ ἱμερόεσσα κρόκην.
ὀγδωκονταέτις δʼ Ἀχερούσιον ηὔγασεν ὕδωρ
ἡ καλὴ καλῶς Πλατθὶς ὑφηναμένη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.731: “ ἄμπελος ὣς ἤδη κάμακι
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
“ ἄμπελος ὣς ἤδη κάμακι στηρίζομαι αὐτῷ
σκηπανίῳ· καλέει μʼ εἰς ἀίδην Θάνατος.
δυσκώφει μὴ Γόργε· τί τοι χαριέστερον, ἢ τρεῖς
ἢ πίσυρας ποίας θάλψαι ὑπʼ ἠελίῳ;”
ὧδʼ εἴπας οὐ κόμπῳ, ἀπὸ ζωὴν ὁ παλαιὸς
ὤσατο, κἠς πλεόνων ἦλθε μετοικεσίην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.736: μὴ φθείρευ, ὤνθρωπε, περιπλάνιον βίον
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
μὴ φθείρευ, ὤνθρωπε, περιπλάνιον βίον ἕλκων,
ἄλλην ἐξ ἄλλης εἰς χθόνʼ ἀλινδόμενος,
μὴ φθείρευ, κἂν εἴ σε περιστέψαιτο καλιὴ
ἣν θάλποι μικκὸν πῦρ ἀνακαιόμενον,
εἰ καί σοι λιτή τε καὶ οὐκ εὐάλφιτος εἴη
φυστὴ ἐνὶ γρώνῃ μασσομένη παλάμαις,
ἢ καί σοι γλήχων, ἢ καὶ θύμον, ἢ καὶ ὁ πικρὸς
ἁδυμιγὴς εἴη χόνδρος ἐποψίδιος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.740: αὐτὰ ἐπὶ Κρήθωνος ἐγὼ λίθος
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
αὐτὰ ἐπὶ Κρήθωνος ἐγὼ λίθος, οὔνομα κείνου
δηλοῦσα· Κρήθων δʼ ἐν χθονίοις σποδιά.
ὁ πρὶν καὶ Γύγῃ παρισεύμενος ὄλβον, ὁ τὸ πρὶν
βουπάμων, ὁ πρὶν πλούσιος αἰπολίοις,
ὁ πρὶν — τί πλείω μυθεῦμαι; ὁ πᾶσι μακαρτός,
φεῦ, γαίης ὅσσης ὅσσον ἔχει μόριον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.24: ἄστρα μὲν ἠμαύρωσε καὶ ἱερὰ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἄστρα μὲν ἠμαύρωσε καὶ ἱερὰ κύκλα σελήνης
ἄξονα δινήσας ἔμπυρος ἠέλιος·
ὑμνοπόλους δʼ ἀγεληδὸν ἀπημάλδυνεν Ὅμηρος,
λαμπρότατον Μουσῶν φέγγος ἀνασχόμενος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.25: γράμμα τόδʼ Ἀρήτοιο δαήμονος, ὅς
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
γράμμα τόδʼ Ἀρήτοιο δαήμονος, ὅς ποτε λεπτῇ
φροντίδι δηναιοὺς ἀστέρας ἐφράσατο,
ἀπλανέας τʼ ἄμφω καὶ ἀλήμονας, οἷσιν ἐναργὴς
ἰλλόμενος κύκλοις οὐρανὸς ἐνδέδεται.
αἰνείσθω δὲ καμὼν ἔργον μέγα, καὶ Διὸς εἶναι
δεύτερος, ὅστις ἔθηκʼ ἄστρα φαεινότερα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.99: Ἴξαλος εὐπώγων αἰγὸς πόσις ἒν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Ἴξαλος εὐπώγων αἰγὸς πόσις ἒν ποθʼ ἁλωῇ
οἴνης τοὺς ἁπαλοὺς πάντας ἔδαψε κλάδους.
τῷ δʼ ἔπος ἐκ γαίης τόσον ἄπυε· “κεῖρε, κάκιστε,
γναθμοῖς ἡμέτερον κλῆμα τὸ καρποφόρον·
ῥίζα γάρ ἔμπεδος οὖσα πάλιν γλυκὺ νέκταρ ἀνήσει,
ὅσσον ἐπισπεῖσαι σοί, τράγε, θυομένῳ.”

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.316: ὦ τάνδε στείχοντες ἀταρπιτόν, αἴτε
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ὦ τάνδε στείχοντες ἀταρπιτόν, αἴτε ποτʼ ἀγροὺς
δαμόθεν, αἴτʼ ἀπʼ ἀγρῶν νεῖσθε ποτʼ ἀκρόπολιν,
ἄμμες ὅρων φύλακες, δισσοὶ θεοί, ὧν ὁ μέν, Ἑρμᾶς,
οἷον ὁρῇς μʼ, οὗτος δʼ ἅτερος, Ἡρακλέης·
ἄμφω μὲν θνατοῖς εὐάκοοι, ἀλλὰ ποθʼ αὑτούς —
αἰ ξύνᾷ παραθῇς ἀχράδας, ἐγκέκαφεν
ναὶ μὰν ὡσαύτως τοὺς βότρυας, αἴτε πέλονται
ὥριμοι, αἴτε χύδαν ὄμφακες, εὐτρέπικεν.
μισέω τὰν μετοχάν, οὐδʼ ἥδομαι· ἀλλʼ ὁ φέρων τι,
ἀμφίς, μὴ κοινᾷ, τοῖς δυσὶ παρτιθέτω,
καὶ λεγέτω· τὶν τοῦθʼ, Ἡράκλεες· ἄλλοτε, “ τοῦτο
Ἑρμᾷ·” καὶ λύοι τὰν ἔριν ἀμφοτέρων.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.318: Εὐμάραθον πρηῶνα καὶ εὐσκάνδικα λελογχώς
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Εὐμάραθον πρηῶνα καὶ εὐσκάνδικα λελογχώς,
Ἑρμῆ, καὶ ταύταν, ἆ φίλος, αἰγίβοσιν,
καὶ λαχανηλόγῳ ἔσσο καὶ αἰγινομῆι προσηνής·
ἕξεις καὶ λαχάνων καὶ γλάγεος μερίδα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.320: εἶπέ ποκʼ Εὐρώτας ποτὶ τὰν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
εἶπέ ποκʼ Εὐρώτας ποτὶ τὰν Κύπριν “ἢ λάβε τεύχη,
ἢ ʼξιθι τᾶς Σπάρτας· ἁ πόλις ὁπλομανεῖ.”
ἁ δʼ ἁπαλὸν γελάσασα, καὶ ἔσσομαι αἰὲν ἀτευχής,
εἶπε, καὶ οἰκήσω τὰν Λακεδαιμονίαν.
χἀμῖν Κύπρις ἄνοπλος· ἀναιδέες οἵδε λέγουσιν
ἵστορες, ὡς ἁμῖν χἀ θεὸς ὁπλοφορεῖ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.322: οὐκ ἐμὰ ταῦτα λάφυρα τίς
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
οὐκ ἐμὰ ταῦτα λάφυρα τίς ὁ θριγκοῖσιν ἀνάψας
Ἄρηος ταύταν τὰν ἄχαριν χάριτα;
ἄθλαστοι μὲν κῶνοι, ἀναίμακτοι δὲ γανῶσαι
ἀσπίδες, ἄκλαστοι δʼ αἱ κλαδαραὶ κάμακες.
αἰδοῖ πάντα πρόσωπʼ ἐρυθαίνομαι, ἐκ δὲ μετώπου
ἱδρὼς πιδύων στῆθος ἐπισταλάει.
παστάδα τις τοιοῖσδε καὶ ἀνδρειῶνα καὶ αὐλὰν
κοσμείτω καὶ τὸν νυμφίδιον θάλαμον
Ἄρευς δʼ αἱματόεντα διωξίπποιο λάφυρα
νηὸν κοσμοίη τοῖς γὰρ ἀρεσκόμεθα,.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.326: πέτρης ἐκ δισσῆς ψυχρὸν κατεπάλμενον
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
πέτρης ἐκ δισσῆς ψυχρὸν κατεπάλμενον ὕδωρ,
χαίροις, καὶ Νυμφέων ποιμενικὰ ξόανα,
πίστραι τε κρηνέων, καὶ ἐν ὕδασι κόσμια ταῦτα
ὑμέων, ὦ κοῦραι, μυρία τεγγόμενα,
χαίρετʼ· Ἀριστοκλεης δʼ ὅδʼ ὁδοιπόρος, ᾧπερ ἀπῶσα
δίψαν βαψάμενος τοῦτο δίδωμι γέρας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.329: νύμφαι ἐφυδριάδες, Δώρου γένος, ἀρδεύοιτε
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
νύμφαι ἐφυδριάδες, Δώρου γένος, ἀρδεύοιτε
τοῦτον Τιμοκλέους κᾶπον ἐπεσσύμεναι·
καὶ γὰρ Τιμοκλέης ὔμμιν, κόραι, αἰὲν ὁ καπεὺς
κάπων ἐκ τούτων ὥρια δωροφορεῖ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.335: Ὑλοφόρου τὠγάλμαθʼ, ὁδοιπόρε, Μικκαλίωνος
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Ὑλοφόρου τὠγάλμαθʼ, ὁδοιπόρε, Μικκαλίωνος·
Ἑρμῆς, ἀλλʼ ἴδε τὸν κρήγυον ὑλοφόρον,
ὡς ἐξ οἰζυρῆς ἠπίστατο δωροδοκῆσαι
ἐργασίης· αἰὲν δʼ ὦ ʼγαθὸς ἐστʼ ἀγαθός.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.337: Εὐάγρει, λαγόθηρα, καὶ εἰ πετεεινὰ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Εὐάγρει, λαγόθηρα, καὶ εἰ πετεεινὰ διώκων
ἰξευτὴς ἥκεις τοῦθʼ ὑπὸ δισσὸν ὄρος,
κἀμὲ τὸν ὑληωρὸν ἀπὸ κρημνοῖο βόασον
Πᾶνα· συναγρεύω καὶ κυσὶ καὶ καλάμοις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.563: τὸν φιλοπωριστὴν Δημόκριτον ἤν που
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τὸν φιλοπωριστὴν Δημόκριτον ἤν που ἐφεύρῃς,
ὤνθρωπʼ, ἄγγειλον τοῦτο τὸ κοῦφον ἔπος,
ὡς ἡ λευκοόπωρος ἐγὼ καὶ ἐφώριος ἤδη
κείνῳ συκοφορῶ τὰς ἀπύρους ἀκόλους·
σπευσάτω, οὐκ ὀχυρὴν γὰρ ἔχω στάσιν, εἴπερ ὀπώρην
ἀβλήτου χρῄζει δρέψαι ἀπʼ ἀκρεμόνος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.719: οὐκ ἔπλασέν με Μύρων, ἐψεύσατο
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
οὐκ ἔπλασέν με Μύρων, ἐψεύσατο· βοσκομέναν δὲ
ἐξ ἀγέλας ἐλάσας, δῆσε βάσει λιθίνῳ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.744: ᾨγινόμοι Σώσων καὶ Σίμαλος, οἱ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ᾨγινόμοι Σώσων καὶ Σίμαλος, οἱ πολύαιγοι,
οἷα βαθυσχίνων, ᾦ ξένε, παρολκίδαν
Ἑρμᾷ τυρευτῆρι καὶ εὔγλαγι τὸν χιμάραρχον
χάλκεον εὐπώγωνʼ ὧδʼ ἀνέθεντο τράγον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca X.1: ὀ πλόος ὡραῖος· καὶ γὰρ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ὀ πλόος ὡραῖος· καὶ γὰρ λαλαγεῦσα χελιδὼν
ἤδη μέμβλωκεν, χὠ χαρίεις Ζέφυρος·
λειμῶνες δʼ ἀνθεῦσι, σεσίγηκεν δὲ θάλασσα
κύμασι καὶ τρηχεῖ πνεύματι βρασσομένη.
ἀγκύρας ἀνέλοιο, καὶ ἐκλύσαιο γύαια,
ναυτίλε, καὶ πλώοις πᾶσαν ἐφεὶς ὀθόνην.
ταῦθʼ ὁ Πρίηπος ἐγὼν ἐπιτέλλομαι ὁ λιμενίτας,
ὤνθρωφʼ, ὡς πλώοις πᾶσαν ἐπʼ ἐμπορίην.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.230: μὴ σὺ γʼ ἐπʼ οἰονόμοιο
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
μὴ σὺ γʼ ἐπʼ οἰονόμοιο περίπλεον ἰλύος ὧδε
τοῦτο χαραδραίης θερμόν, ὁδῖτα, πίῃς·
ἀλλὰ μολὼν μάλα τυτθὸν ὑπὲρ δαμαλήβοτον ἄκραν
ταύταν, πὰρ κείνᾳ ποιμενίᾳ πίτυϊ
εὑρήσεις κελαρύζον ἐϋκρήνου διὰ πέτρης
νᾶμα, Βορειαίης ψυχρότερον νιφάδος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VI.154: Ἀγρονόμῳ τάδε Πανὶ καὶ εὐαστῆρι
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Ἀγρονόμῳ τάδε Πανὶ καὶ εὐαστῆρι Λυαίῳ
πρέσβυς καὶ Νύμφαις Ἀρκὰς ἔθηκε Βίτων
Πανὶ μὲν ἀρτίτοκον χίμαρον συμπαίστορα ματρός,
κισσοῦ δὲ Βρομίῳ κλῶνα πολυπλανέος·
νύμφαις δὲ σκιερῆς εὐποίκιλον ἄνθος ὀπώρης,
φύλλα τε πεπταμένων αἱματόεντα ῥόδων.
ἀνθʼ ὧν εὔυδρον, Νύμφαι, τόδε δῶμα γέροντος
αὔξετε, Πὰν γλαγερόν, Βάκχε πολυστάφυλον

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.19: τὸν χαρίεντʼ Ἀλκμᾶνα, τὸν ὑμνητῆρʼ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τὸν χαρίεντʼ Ἀλκμᾶνα, τὸν ὑμνητῆρʼ ὑμεναίων
κύκνον, τὸν Μουσῶν ἄξια μελψάμενον,
τύμβος ἔχει, Σπάρτας μεγάλαν χάριν, εἰθʼ ὅ γε λοῖσθος
ἄχθος ἀπορρίψας οἴχεται εἰς Ἀίδαν.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.35: ἄρμενος ἦν ξείνοισιν ἀνὴρ ὅδε
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἄρμενος ἦν ξείνοισιν ἀνὴρ ὅδε καὶ φίλος ἀστοῖς,
Πίνδαρος, εὐφώνων Πιερίδων· πρόπολος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.67: Ἀίδεω λυπηρὲ διήκονε, τοῦτʼ Ἀχέροντος
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Ἀίδεω λυπηρὲ διήκονε, τοῦτʼ Ἀχέροντος
ὕδωρ ὃς πλώεις πορθμίδι κυανέῃ,
δέξαι μʼ, εἰ καί σοι μέγα βρίθεται ὀκρυόεσσα
βᾶρις ἀποφθιμένων, τὸν κύνα Διογένην.
ὄλπη μοι καὶ πήρη ἐφόλκια, καὶ τὸ παλαιὸν
ἔσθος, χὠ φθιμένους ναυστολέων ὀβολός.
πάνθʼ ὅσα κἠν ζωοῖς ἐπεπάμεθα, ταῦτα παρʼ ᾍδαν
ἔρχομʼ ἔχων λείπω δʼ οὐδὲν ὑπʼ ἠελίῳ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.173: αὐτόμαται δείλῃ ποτὶ ταὔλιον αἱ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
αὐτόμαται δείλῃ ποτὶ ταὔλιον αἱ βόες ἦλθον
ἐξ ὄρεος, πολλῇ νιφόμεναι χιόνι·
αἰαῖ, Θηρίμαχος δὲ παρὰ δρυῒ τὸν μακρὸν εὕδει
ὕπνον ἐκοιμήθη δʼ ἐκ πυρὸς οὐρανίου.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.190: Ἀκρίδι τᾷ κατʼ ἄρουραν ἀηδόνι
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Ἀκρίδι τᾷ κατʼ ἄρουραν ἀηδόνι, καὶ δρυοκοίτᾳ
τέττιγι ξυνὸν τύμβον ἔτευξε Μυρώ,
παρθένιον στάξασα κόρα δάκρυ· δισσὰ γὰρ αὐτᾶς
παίγνιʼ ὁ δυσπειθὴς ᾤχετʼ ἔχων Ἀίδας.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.659: νήπιον υἱὸν ἔλειπες· ἐν ἡλικίῃ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
νήπιον υἱὸν ἔλειπες· ἐν ἡλικίῃ δὲ καὶ αὐτός,
Εὐρύμεδον, τύμβου τοῦδε θανὼν ἔτυχες.
σοὶ μὲν ἕδρη θείοισι παρʼ ἀνδράσι· τὸν δὲ πολῖται
τιμησεῦντι, πατρὸς μνώμενοι ὡς ἀγαθοῦ.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.107: τὴν μικρήν με λέγουσι, καὶ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τὴν μικρήν με λέγουσι, καὶ οὐκ ἴσα ποντοπορεύσαις
ναυσὶ διιθύνειν ἄτρομον εὐπλοΐην
οὐκ ἀπόφημι δʼ ἐγώ· βραχὺ μὲν σκάφος, ἀλλὰ θαλάσσῃ
πᾶν ἴσον οὐ μέτρων ἡ κρίσις, ἀλλὰ τύχης.
ἔστω πηδαλίοις ἑτέρῃ πλέον ἄλλο γὰρ ἄλλῃ
θάρσος· ἐγὼ δʼ εἴην δαίμοσι σῳζομένη.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca IX.179: Τοξοβόλον τὸν Ἔρωτα τίς ἔξεσεν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Τοξοβόλον τὸν Ἔρωτα τίς ἔξεσεν ἐκ λιβανωτοῦ,
τόν ποτε μηδʼ αὐτοῦ Ζηνὸς ἀποσχόμενον;
ὀψέ ποθʼ Ἡφαίστῳ κεῖται σκοπός, ὃν καθορᾶσθαι
ἔπρεπεν οὐκ ἄλλως ἢ πυρὶ τυφόμενον.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.171: Ἄρεος ἔντεα ταῦτα τίνος χάριν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Ἄρεος ἔντεα ταῦτα τίνος χάριν, ὦ Κυθέρεια,
ἐνδέδυσαι, κενεὸν τοῦτο φέρουσα βάρος;
αὐτὸν Ἄρη γυμνὴ γὰρ ἀφώπλισας· εἰ δὲ λέλειπται
καὶ θεός, ἀνθρώποις ὅπλα μάτην ἐπάγεις.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.182: τὰν ἐκφυγοῦσαν ματρὸς ἐκ κόλπων
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τὰν ἐκφυγοῦσαν ματρὸς ἐκ κόλπων, ἔτι
ἀφρῷ τε μορμύρουσαν, εὐλεχῆ Κύπριν
ἰδὼν Ἀπελλῆς, κάλλος ἱμερώτατον,
οὐ γραπτόν, ἀλλʼ ἔμψυχον ἐξεμάξατο.
εὖ μὲν γὰρ ἄκραις χερσὶν ἐκθλίβει κόμαν,
εὖ δʼ ὀμμάτων γαληνὸς ἐκλάμπει πόθος,
καὶ μαζός, ἀκμῆς ἄγγελος, κυδωνιᾷ·
αὐτὰ δʼ Ἀθάνα καὶ Διὸς συνευνέτις
φάσουσιν ὦ Ζεῦ, λειπόμεσθα τῇ κρίσει.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.190: τᾶν αἰγῶν ὁ νομεὺς Μόριχος
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
τᾶν αἰγῶν ὁ νομεὺς Μόριχος τὸν ἐπίσκοπον Ἑρμᾶν
ἔστασ’ αἰπολίων εὐδόκιμον φύλακα.
ἀλλά μοι αἳ τʼ ἀνʼ ὄρη χλωρᾶς κεκορεσμέναι ὕλας,
τοῦ γʼ ἁρπακτῆρος μή τι μέλεσθε λύκου.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.206: Θεσπιέες τὸν Ἔρωτα μόνον θεὸν
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
Θεσπιέες τὸν Ἔρωτα μόνον θεὸν ἐκ Κυθερείης
ἅζοντʼ, οὐχ ἑτέρου γραπτὸν ἀπʼ ἀρχετύπου,
ἀλλʼ ὃν Πραξιτέλης ἔγνω θεόν· ὃν περὶ Φρύνῃ
δερκόμενος, σφετέρων λύτρον ἔδωκε πόθων

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.261: ἀμφοτέραις παρʼ ὁδοῖσι φύλαξ ἕστηκα
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἀμφοτέραις παρʼ ὁδοῖσι φύλαξ ἕστηκα Πρίηπος,
ἰθυτενὲς μηρῶν ὀρθιάσας ῥόπαλον.
εἵσατο γὰρ πιστόν με Θεόκριτος· ἀλλʼ ἀποτηλοῦ
φὼρ ἴθι, μὴ κλαύσῃς τὴν φλέβα δεξάμενος.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.306: πρέσβυν Ἀνακρείοντα χύδαν σεσαλαγμένον οἴνῳ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
πρέσβυν Ἀνακρείοντα χύδαν σεσαλαγμένον οἴνῳ
θάεο δινωτοῦ στρεπτὸν ὕπερθε λίθου,
ὡς ὁ γέρων λίχνοισιν ἐπʼ ὄμμασιν ὑγρὰ δεδορκὼς
ἄχρι καὶ ἀστραγάλων ἕλκεται ἀμπεχόναν·
δισσῶν δʼ ἀρβυλίδων τὰν μὲν μίαν, οἷα μεθυπλήξ,
ὤλεσεν· ἐν δʼ ἑτέρᾳ ῥικνὸν ἄραρε πόδα.
μέλπει δʼ ἠὲ Βάθυλλον ἐφίμερον, ἠὲ Μεγιστέα,
αἰωρῶν παλάμᾳ τὰν δυσέρωτα χέλυν.
ἀλλὰ πάτερ Διόνυσε, φύλασσέ μιν οὐ γὰρ ἔοικεν
ἐκ Βάκχου πίπτειν Βακχιακὸν θέραπα.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca XVI.307: ἴδʼ ὡς ὁ πρέσβυς ἐκ
poems.author: Leonidas of Tarentum
poems.text:
ἴδʼ ὡς ὁ πρέσβυς ἐκ μέθας Ἀνακρέων
ὑπεσκέλισται, καὶ τὸ λῶπος ἕλκεται
ἐσάχρι γυίων τῶν δὲ βλαυτίων τὸ μὲν
ὅμως φυλάσσει, θάτερον δʼ ἀπώλεσεν.
μελίσδεται δὲ τὰν χέλυν διακρέκων
ἤτοι Βάθυλλον, ἢ καλὸν Μεγιστέα.
φύλασσε, Βάκχε, τὸν γέροντα, μὴ πέσῃ.
